articles.title: The former youth pastor leading one of the NFL’s best offenses
articles.summary: Nate Scheelhaase, the Los Angeles Rams’ offensive coordinator, is a former youth pastor. He credits time in the church for his success in professional football.
articles.body: When Nate Scheelhaase was promoted to offensive coordinator of the Los Angeles Rams last winter, he stepped into one of the NFL’s most auspicious jobs, and for a Super Bowl contender, no less. Not bad for a former youth pastor. Fresh out of college, Scheelhaase moved to Louisville, Kentucky, in 2014 to work with teenagers at Southeast Christian Church, one of the largest megachurches in the U.S. During that time, he regularly stopped by a few dozen high schools to visit with students. For two high schools’ football teams, he volunteered as a chaplain. The role entailed building trust, finding common ground and helping those he spoke with work for something bigger than themselves. “An impactful year,” said Scheelhaase, 35. It wasn’t the typical starting point for a career in coaching — because even though Scheelhaase had been a four-year starting quarterback at Illinois, he wasn’t initially interested in that career path at all. Without intending to, though, Scheelhaase honed skills while he was a youth pastor that he says helped him rise quickly within the coaching industry. “I would say that there’s a lot of carryover,” Scheelhaase said in an interview. “From a ministry standpoint, just being around people from all different walks of life, different journeys, being able to meet them where they’re at — that’s also a football locker room. That’s a staff locker room.” The growth of sports in the U.S. is often a story of their crossover with faith. James Naismith, basketball’s inventor, is said to have believed he could better embody what it meant to be a Christian using sports than the pulpit. Many of football’s conventions, including the huddle, numbered jerseys and padded goalposts, came from Amos Alonzo Stagg, who had gone to Yale to study divinity and began coaching to fulfill a vision of “muscular Christianity.” Careers in sports have often led to careers in religious roles. Rocky Seto won national championships at the University of Southern California and a Super Bowl with the Seattle Seahawks during 16 years on Pete Carroll’s coaching staffs. In Seattle, Seto’s role eventually evolved to include a weekly address delivered in front of the entire roster and staff. He obsessively prepared his material. “How am I going to capture the whole room?” Seto said. “It’s basically convincing them that if you learn this, this is going to help us win, help us be better.” That experience made him feel prepared to give his first sermon. It was 2017, and Seto had just left the Seahawks to become the pastor-in-waiting at Evergreen Baptist Church, in suburban Los Angeles. Standing in front of another packed room of congregants, Seto felt his new job’s mission mirrored that of his last one — to deliver hope. “You come to church in some ways to take a peek into heaven for a moment, and then we break. It’s like a huddle, and then we break out to basically fulfill the Great Commission outside this building, right?” he said. “And so coaching is no different. The information has to be almost like, ‘This is the greatest thing you need to know.’” As Scheelhaase’s career was ending in late 2013, all he knew was that he didn’t envision a future in coaching. He had gotten married a few months earlier, and he had seen enough coaches get fired and hired to question raising a family in an industry with fleeting job security and a nomadic career path. Meetings with Illini alumni in corporate jobs in Chicago also failed to inspire him. Unsure what to do, Scheelhaase called Jason Epperson, a local pastor who served as Illinois football’s team chaplain. Epperson had just taken a job at Southeast in Louisville, where there was a youth pastor role open. The idea intrigued Scheelhaase, who had grown up outside Kansas City, Missouri, as a devout Christian. When he arrived at Southeast in early 2014, he was trying “to figure out different ways to just connect with people in the area and show them that I was interested in just who they were more than just what they were doing,” Scheelhaase said. “Which I think is always a good spot to start.” Chris Burke, an ESPN baseball analyst who lived in the area, first noticed Scheelhaase because of his athleticism during pickup games inside Southeast’s gym. Other things about Scheelhaase soon stood out, too. “He looked perfectly suited for that job,” Burke said. “You can tell he got a kick out of being around young people. He communicated well with them. He had the patience.” When a local mother told Scheelhaase that her eighth grade son’s father had recently died and that she needed others to be there for her son, Scheelhaase gave him rides and went to practices. The son was Nate Hobbs, the future San Francisco 49ers defensive back whom Scheelhaase still describes as one of his closest friends. Scheelhaase stopped by Trinity High School, a local powerhouse, with a “confident humility,” said Andrew Coverdale, Trinity’s offensive coordinator at the time, who is now the passing game coordinator at Kentucky. Scheelhaase didn’t expect students to listen to him just because he had been a college quarterback. “As somebody who taught in high school for a long, long time, I can’t really emphasize enough that kids need every form of mentorship and positive adult presence they can have, because it is brutal to be a teenage kid right now,” Coverdale said. High schoolers are “just dealing with so much and carrying so much. And so I just think having a guy like that around that you can talk to, who has life experience that he’s willing to share in a really winsome way, it was just great.” Scheelhaase spent a relatively brief year and a half in Louisville, but he said that time shaped him immeasurably. Scheelhaase, who now has three children, said spending time around church leaders and attendees gave him role models for how he wanted to act as a husband and a father. It also changed his career path. While he was leading a chapel service for football players at Eastern High School in 2014, he gave what he thought was a compelling, relatable speech that pulled in his athletic background and life story. It was received, he said with a smile, by proverbial crickets. Taking a seat, he was stunned to see the reaction when the school’s head coach stood up to deliver his own pregame speech. “Everybody was on the edge of their seat,” Scheelhaase said. “And in that moment, I thought, man, there is a cool ability to impact as a coach. And it was probably the thing that triggered the thought of, man, what would it look like to be able to impact in that way and influence in that way.” By the start of the 2015 football season, Scheelhaase was at Illinois coaching running backs. Technically, he was new to the profession. Yet recruiting players to campus and developing them once they were on the roster didn’t feel any different, at its core, from how he’d worked to build trust in Louisville. “You are going to ask people to do really hard things as a coach, things that are counterintuitive to what you want to do,” he said. “Stand in a pocket where you know somebody’s going to hit you in the side of your helmet. To be somebody who loves to catch the football, but you got to go and block. To be somebody that’s willing to do the dirty work, and you’re going to ask them to do it, and the only way I know how to do that is to connect with them on a deep level. They know I not only understand what we’re asking them to do, but I care and I see them in that. And so connection, fortunately for me, it’s how I’m wired. That’s the part I enjoy the most about my job. ... “And there probably is an element of that’s what I enjoyed even about the job as a high school pastor in Louisville, too, is just connecting with people and seeing there’s oftentimes more common ground than you think.” In 2023, he became a coordinator at Iowa State. A year later, he left to become an offensive assistant for Sean McVay and the Rams, which to some may have seemed like a backward step; his job revolved around using software to manually draw the plays McVay wanted called each week. In the NFL, however, just being around McVay is a career springboard: The last four Rams offensive coordinators are now head coaches, and Zac Taylor was drawing McVay’s plays before Cincinnati hired him as its head coach. In 2025, a full year before Scheelhaase’s promotion to Rams offensive coordinator, McVay had called him “a special coach” and “a rising star, without a doubt.” Last winter, as Scheelhaase was interviewing for NFL head coaching jobs, he called interim Stanford coach Frank Reich to ask about the school’s opening. The two had more in common than football. After he retired from a long career as a backup NFL quarterback, Reich attended seminary and worked as a pastor before he became an NFL head coach. He saw carryover between the two industries, too. “In coaching or seminary or pastoring, there are a lot of hours,” Reich said in 2019. The hours Scheelhaase put in in Louisville have paid off in ways he didn’t expect, he said. There, his life revolved around Sundays. In ways he could never have predicted, it still does.

articles.title: B/R's Week 8 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings
articles.summary: With seven weeks of the 2026 NFL season complete, the fantasy regular season has reached its midpoint in many leagues.
articles.body:
With seven weeks of the 2026 NFL season complete, the fantasy regular season has reached its midpoint in many leagues.

For some managers, it has been a strong start: Their draft picks have delivered, their rosters have avoided major injuries, and they're well-positioned to compete for a playoff spot.

For others, 2026 has been a nightmare. Even players who have stayed healthy have fallen short of expectations, losses have piled up and playoff hopes are fading.

Whether you're protecting a strong record or trying to turn your season around, Bleacher Report can help with your Week 8 lineup decisions through position-by-position PPR rankings, player notes, start-or-sit recommendations and sleepers.

Before we get things going for Week 8 with a set of sortable PPR player rankings, a few notes.

The first is the same as always. The list of the top 124 players overall can help fantasy managers in making "flex" calls. However, it does not contain quarterbacks. If you play in a "superflex" format where QBs are flex-eligible and you have a decent second signal-caller on the roster, he belongs in a flex spot.

The second is that the byes continue this week. The Houston Texans, New York Giants, New Orleans Saints and San Francisco 49ers are all off. So, no Christian McCaffrey or Nico Collins in Week 8.

Finally, whether you are 5-2 or 2-5, it's easy to look ahead to the playoffs or feel overwhelmed by the ground you need to make up. Keep your immediate focus on Week 8, especially if you're trying to turn your season around.

Treat this week's slate like a playoff matchup: Focus on the lineup decisions that give you the best chance to win now. Take that approach each week and work toward putting together a winning streak.

Jared Goff continues to outperform his fantasy draft position.

Last year, the Detroit Lions quarterback finished the season second in the NFL in both passing yards (4,564) and touchdown passes (34), but a Week 17 clunker knocked him outside the top 10 in fantasy points . Over the summer, he was the 16th quarterback selected on average .

Fantasy managers who drafted Goff late have received excellent value so far. He leads the league in passing yards per game (298.0), ranks third in touchdown passes (14) and has yet to throw an interception. Only Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is averaging more fantasy points per game.

Fantasy managers were thrown a curveball last week when Lamar Jackson of the Baltimore Ravens (ankle) was a late scratch—a move that reportedly left even the Ravens " shocked ."

With Baltimore sitting in the AFC North cellar and facing arguably the best team in the AFC in the Bills in Week 8, it needs Jackson back under center as badly as fantasy managers do.

One injured quarterback did return to action in Week 7. Baker Mayfield of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers was out there against the Carolina Panthers after missing multiple games with a thumb injury. That injury appears to still be an issue, though. He completed just seven passes and threw for all of 64 yards.

Over the first six weeks of the 2026 season, Bryce Young of the Carolina Panthers was a top-five fantasy quarterback. But he came crashing back to Earth in last Sunday's loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, with 163 passing yards, one touchdown and three turnovers. He is a low-end QB1 at best Thursday night in Green Bay.

Dak Prescott, Dallas Cowboys (vs. Arizona Cardinals)

Prescott broke out of his mini-slump in last week's win over the Philadelphia Eagles, throwing for 212 yards and three touchdowns. He should build on that success at home Sunday against the Cardinals—Arizona has given up the second-most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.

Caleb Williams, Chicago Bears (at Seattle Seahawks)

When Williams and the Bears offense have been at their best, they have been unstoppable. But Chicago faces a daunting task this week in Seattle against the Seahawks and their "Dark Side" defense. Seattle just totally stymied the Chiefs, and only the Minnesota Vikings have been a worse fantasy matchup for quarterbacks in 2026.

Kyler Murray, Minnesota Vikings (at Detroit Lions)

A trendy value pick over the summer, Murray has fallen short of expectations this season. This week's matchup at Ford Field offers the eighth-year veteran a prime opportunity to rebound—the Lions are the only team in the league allowing more than 25 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.

Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs was the first overall pick in quite a few fantasy drafts this summer, and managers who lucked into that pick have been reaping the benefits.

Despite Detroit having already had its bye week, Gibbs leads the NFL with 166 touches. He has tallied almost 900 total yards and leads the league with nine touchdowns.

In news that should surprise no one, he leads all running backs in PPR points. He has also been robotically consistent—Gibbs has at least 15 PPR points in every game this season.

The good news for Saquon Barkley fantasy managers is that he was back out there Monday night after missing time with a hamstring injury, logging 71 total yards and a touchdown. The bad news was that you can count his snaps against Dallas on both hands, his hamstring clearly isn't right and now he has a back injury to boot.

Barkley wasn't the only back who got dinged up in Week 7. Christian McCaffrey of the San Francisco 49ers and Cam Skattebo of the New York Giants both suffered hamstring injuries, while Aaron Jones Sr. of the Minnesota Vikings sprained his knee. McCaffrey and Skattebo have Week 8 off, but Jones appears set to miss time.

Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty has struggled on the ground this season, averaging just over three yards per carry. As he did as a rookie, however, the second-year pro has remained productive as a receiver, helping him rank among the top 10 running backs in total PPR points.

Josh Jacobs, Green Bay Packers (vs. Carolina Panthers)

Jacobs saw his first game action of 2026 last week against the Detroit Lions, turning 16 touches into 91 yards and a touchdown. Thursday's home date with the Panthers is the perfect time for the Packers to get their floundering ground game going—Carolina has allowed a whopping 153.2 yards per game on the ground.

Jonathan Taylor, Indianapolis Colts (at Jacksonville Jaguars)

This assumes that Taylor is still on the roster come Sunday, which isn't a given after All-Pro guard Quentin Nelson was traded. But even if Taylor is out there, the sledding will be tough. The Jaguars led the league in run defense in 2025 and are right back in that spot this season.

Bam Knight, Arizona Cardinals (at Dallas Cowboys)

With Jeremiyah Love on the shelf with a high-ankle sprain, Knight has been splitting time in the backfield with Tyler Allgeier. The last two weeks at least, it's Knight who has been the more effective runner, and this week the Cardinals face a Cowboys defense allowing the eighth-most PPR points to running backs this year.

Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown is soaring once again this season.

Last week's win over the Green Bay Packers was the second time this season that the 27-year-old has caught nine passes and eclipsed 140 receiving yards.

Jameson Williams got the touchdowns, but St. Brown is still tied for third in the league with five scores and sits fourth among wideouts in both PPR points and points per game.

Granted, the 2021 fourth-rounder isn't rampaging across the NFL like Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who is almost 40 points clear of the No. 2 wideout in points.

But just like Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs, fantasy managers who drafted St. Brown have no complaints at this point in the season.

Injuries continue to mount at wide receiver. Denver Broncos wideout Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Seattle Seahawks wideout Rashid Shaheed (knee) both suffered injuries last week, leaving their Week 8 availability uncertain.

New York Jets rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. has topped 100 receiving yards in each of his last two games. Teammate Garrett Wilson, meanwhile, has struggled to produce, totaling just six catches for 70 yards over that span.

Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Tre Tucker was a late-round dart throw in most fantasy drafts, but he ranks among the top 15 wideouts in total PPR points this season. He caught five passes for 103 yards and a touchdown against the Rams last week, marking his third game with more than 20 PPR points.

Stefon Diggs, Washington Commanders (vs. Philadelphia Eagles)

With Terry McLaurin out for the season after rupturing the patellar tendon in his knee, Diggs comes out of Washington's bye week as the Commanders' No. 1 wide receiver. That should mean good things under the lights this week against the Eagles, who have surrendered the second-most PPR points per game to wide receivers.

Luther Burden III, Chicago Bears (at Seattle Seahawks)

Last week against the New England Patriots, Burden went off (again) to the tune of four catches for a season-high 130 yards and a touchdown. Backing those numbers up is going to be difficult this week in Seattle—no team has given up fewer PPR points per game to wide receivers this season.

Ja'Kobi Lane, Baltimore Ravens (at Buffalo Bills)

Lane has shown some flashes during his rookie season, and he was one of fantasy's biggest training camp hype darlings. This week the hype and the production should come together in Buffalo—seven weeks into the 2026 season, the Bills are giving up a whopping 42.3 PPR points per game to wideouts.

Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta made news last week when he expressed frustration over the lack of a contract extension during an appearance on the Pardon My Take podcast (h/t ESPN ).

"I'm going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's going to be all good," he said. "I'll go get paid somewhere else. So, whatever."

The 25-year-old had a quiet outing on National Tight Ends Day this past Sunday, finishing with one catch for 18 yards on two targets.

Still, LaPorta is a top-five tight end in PPR points—and odds are when the dust settles, he'll get his payday from the Lions.

Trey McBride of the Arizona Cardinals is a valuable fantasy asset.

Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is averaging slightly more PPR points per game, but McBride leads the position in total PPR points through seven weeks. McBride is also tied for second in the league in targets, and no player has more receptions.

For most of the first month of the 2026 season, Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland was barely involved in the offense. Recently, however, the 2025 No. 10 pick has become a more frequent target for Caleb Williams. The second-year pro caught seven passes for 69 yards and a touchdown last week and has scored at least 18.5 PPR points in back-to-back games.

While Loveland is finally heating up for fantasy managers, Travis Kelce of the Kansas City Chiefs has been in a prolonged funk. In Week 2, Kelce posted a 9/101/1 stat line and topped 25 PPR points. In his last three games combined, however, Kelce has just 21.2 fantasy points.

T.J. Hockenson, Minnesota Vikings (at Detroit Lions)

The Vikings offense isn't exactly lighting it up, but Hockenson has been quietly solid for fantasy managers. His 13.5-point PPR performance in Week 7 marked his second double-digit effort in three games. The Lions have been a fantasy goldmine for opposing tight ends this season.

Sam LaPorta, Detroit Lions (vs. Minnesota Vikings)

LaPorta faces a difficult matchup as he looks to rebound from last week's quiet outing. The Vikings are allowing fewer than seven PPR points per game to tight ends in 2026, limiting his fantasy outlook for Sunday's NFC North showdown.

Mason Taylor, New York Jets (vs. Las Vegas Raiders)

Jets quarterback Geno Smith has frequently targeted Taylor over the past two weeks. Taylor has totaled nine catches for 95 yards and two touchdowns on 12 targets during that span. He could build on that production in Week 8 against the Raiders, who have allowed the fourth-most PPR points per game to tight ends this season.

Harrison Butker is enduring an unusually difficult season.

For his entire 10-year career, the 31-year-old has been the kicker for the Kansas City Chiefs. He has won three Super Bowls with the team and led the NFL in scoring. In 2023, he missed just two of 35 field-goal attempts.

He missed that many last week against the Seattle Seahawks.

It's a continuation of a dismal season for Butker—he has whiffed on five of 16 field goal attempts, and his make percentage is south of 70 percent.

While speaking to reporters , Chiefs head coach Andy Reid conceded that something has to change.

"He's been one of the most consistent kickers in football, but he's off a bit, so we've got to fix it," he said.

If the misses keep piling up, Butker could go from being one of the league's better-known kickers to being out of a job.

Seven weeks into the 2026 season, the Minnesota Vikings are fantasy's highest-scoring defense. They are piling up the points by being ridiculously aggressive.

After blitzing on over 80 percent of Daniel Jones' dropbacks in Week 7, the Vikings' blitz rate is a jaw-dropping 71.4 percent . Only one other team has a blitz rate over 45 percent, and no other team is sending an extra guy half the time.

Houston's defense is no longer a reliable weekly fantasy starter. Last year, the Texans were one of the league's best defenses from both an NFL and fantasy perspective. After last week's overtime loss to the New York Giants, they are 18th in total defense and 19th in fantasy points among defenses.

After bringing in veteran Brandon McManus, the Los Angeles Rams are on their third kicker of the season. McManus attempted only extra points against the Raiders last week, leaving him without a field-goal opportunity in that matchup.

Los Angeles Rams Defense (vs. Los Angeles Chargers)

To say the Rams have been a disappointment defensively this season is an understatement. This is their last chance to produce for fantasy managers against a Chargers team leading the league in fantasy points allowed to defenses this year.

Cam Little, Jacksonville Jaguars (vs. Indianapolis Colts)

Little draws a favorable matchup against the Colts this week, who are the only team in the league allowing at least 10 fantasy points per game to kickers in 2026.

Minnesota Vikings Defense (at Detroit Lions)

The Vikings have been playing excellent defense this season, but Sunday brings the biggest test of the season. The Lions are dead-last in fantasy points per game allowed to defenses this season.

Jason Myers, Seattle Seahawks (vs. Chicago Bears)

Myers is one of the more reliable kickers in the league, and he has hit on 93.3 percent of his field-goal attempts in 2026. But this week's matchup with the Bears is a shaky one in terms of fantasy points surrendered to kickers.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers Defense (vs. Atlanta Falcons)

Tampa was dominant defensively last week against the Carolina Panthers, posting the best fantasy number of the week. The Bucs have the NFC's top run defense. And the Falcons are giving up the third-most fantasy points per game to defenses.

Andre Szmyt, Cleveland Browns (at Pittsburgh Steelers)

Szmyt has delivered several game-winning kicks this season. In his first meeting with the Steelers, he made field goals from 44 and 56 yards and converted all three extra-point attempts.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: Week 8 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Advice for Fringe Flex Fantasy Football Starters
articles.summary: As is the case in the NFL, fantasy football managers cannot simply rely on their biggest stars each and every week. This is, in part, because bye weeks are a hindrance in fantasy instead of a welcome break.
articles.body:
As is the case in the NFL, fantasy football managers cannot simply rely on their biggest stars each and every week. This is, in part, because bye weeks are a hindrance in fantasy instead of a welcome break.

The Houston Texans, New Orleans Saints, New York Giants, and San Francisco 49ers will be off in Week 8. This means the managers of players like Nico Collins, Chris Olave, Malik Nabers, and Christian McCaffrey may have to rely on fringe starters to make it through the week.

Here, you'll find start/sit recommendations for some of the top fringe flex options, based on past production, upcoming matchups, projected role, and point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

New York Jets running back Braelon Allen has been a fill-in for Breece Hall as the latter recovers from a quad injury. Hall appeared close to returning for Week 7, and there's a very real chance that he'll be back for Week 8. However, managers should expect to see Allen retain a sizeable workload.

The Jets won't want to overload Hall in his first game back, and with Allen playing extremely well, they'll have no reason to do so. The third-year back has averaged 4.6 yards per carry this season and has topped 12 fantasy points in three straight games.

Allen delivered a season-high 19.4 fantasy points last week and could have similar production this week, even in a dual-backfield role.

The Jets are set to host the Las Vegas Raiders, who have surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing running backs this season.

J.K. Dobbins rewarded fantasy managers with a touchdown run in Week 7, but logged just six carries for 23 yards on the day. The Denver Broncos' backfield rotation makes him a very risky play moving forward and an avoidable choice in Week 8.

RJ Harvey has emerged as Denver's top receiving back, and rookie Jonah Coleman is starting to gain traction as a potential leading rusher.

"Got to get him more touches," head coach Sean Payton said after Coleman's nine-carry, 54-yard outing in Week 7, per Susanna Weir of the team's official website.

Dobbins will undoubtedly maintain a role in the backfield rotation, but his floor is low, and he faces a tough Week 8 matchup. The Kansas City Chiefs have surrendered the eighth-fewest fantasy points to opposing running backs.

Start: Michael Wilson, WR, Arizona Cardinals

Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Michael Wilson was a veritable must-start last season, but he has cooled off considerably in 2026, especially recently.

Wilson did deliver 10.6 fantasy points in Week 7, but he failed to reach double digits in Weeks 5 and 6. He spiked with a 25.9-point outing in Week 2 and has averaged fewer than 10 fantasy points in his other six games this season.

However, managers should trust Wilson this week in a favorable matchup with the Dallas Cowboys. While Dallas' defense showed some signs of life on Monday night, it still can't be considered good.

Dallas has surrendered the sixth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers this season.

Sit: A.J. Brown, WR, New England Patriots

The Miami Dolphins' inability to defend the run consistently has led opposing teams to regularly attack them on the ground. This is a big part of the reason why Miami has been problematic for some receivers in fantasy.

Jets rookie Omar Cooper Jr. had a strong outing against the Dolphins last week, but Miami held No. 1 receiver Garrett Wilson to just two catches for 26 yards.

In all, Miami has surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers this season.

This is a matchup that doesn't bode well for New England Patriots receiver A.J. Brown, who was supposed to be a weekly must-start in PPR formats. Brown failed to develop a connection with Drake Maye, has yet to reach seven fantasy points in a game, and will draw a ton of attention from the Dolphins' defense on Sunday.

*Fantasy scoring information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: 2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 8
articles.summary: We're now less than two weeks away from the NFL's November 10 trade deadline, and fans can expect the trade activity to ramp up in the coming days.
articles.body:
We're now less than two weeks away from the NFL's November 10 trade deadline, and fans can expect the trade activity to ramp up in the coming days.

While the Los Angeles Chargers are the only remaining winless team, several other squads have slowly slipped out of the playoff picture. This doesn't guarantee that they'll be sellers at the deadline, of course, but for teams that can't legitimately contend, selling off veterans is often logical.

Which marquee players are most likely to be available via the trade market? Who are the top options for contenders to target? That's what we're here to examine ahead of Week 8.

Here, you'll find our updated list of top 10 trade candidates, ranked according to factors like recent production, player upside, positional value, contract/cap implications, projected availability, and any relevant recent rumors.

You'll also find projected trade values based on factors such as position, player upside, player age, and any comparable deals, along with sensible potential suitors for each player.

Projected Trade Value: 2027 4th-Round Pick

The Tennessee Titans have seen glimmers of hope over the past two weeks. However, they still fell to 1-6 with Sunday's loss to the Cleveland Browns and should be looking ahead to the future.

The Titans should be interested in putting more pieces around second-year quarterback Cam Ward, and they may want to trade away some defensive pieces before November 10 to help do it. Safety Amani Hooker would be a prime candidate in that scenario.

While Hooker is signed through 2028, he may not be cemented in Tennessee's long-term plans. He's set to carry a cap hit of $13.2 million in 2027, and releasing him in the spring would save $7.4 million in cap space.

Hooker has been a solid starter for the Titans and is still only 28 years old. He's allowed an opposing passer rating of just 81.2 in coverage this season, and he would undoubtedly draw interest from teams in need of secondary help.

Potential Suitors: Buffalo Bills, Washington Commanders

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 5th-Round Pick

Defensive lineman Zach Sieler is a leader in the Miami Dolphins' young locker room, and, according to agent Drew Rosenhaus, there hasn't been any talk of Sieler getting traded yet.

"I have not had any discussion with the Dolphins or any other team about [him] being traded," Rosenhaus told WSVN (h/t David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel ). "There had been no discussions about that."

Still, Sieler would be a very logical trade chip for Miami. He's 31, and he's a potential 2027 cap casualty.

$10 million of Sieler's 2027 salary will become fully guaranteed on the third day of the new league year. Releasing him with a post-June 1 designation before then would save the Dolphins $13.2 million in cap space.

While the Dolphins did pick up their first win of the season in Week 7, they're not a playoff team. Sieler, who has 17 tackles and two sacks this season, would be a great fit for a team that can make the postseason.

Potential Suitors: Carolina Panthers, Green Bay Packers

8. Jauan Jennings, WR, Minnesota Vikings

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 6th-Round Pick and/or Backfield Help

The Minnesota Vikings are the last remaining undefeated team, but they could still consider moving an expendable piece to address an area of need. Specifically, they might try to add a running back, as Aaron Jones continues to deal with an MCL sprain .

Jauan Jennings is a player the Vikings could try to move. Minnesota signed him to a one-year, $8 million deal in the offseason, but he has not been heavily utilized in the offense to this point.

Jennings has just four catches for 43 yards in five appearances.

ESPN's Adam Schefter told The Pat McAfee Show (beginning at the 1:35:10 mark) on Tuesday that while it doesn't sound like any trade is imminent, teams have "checked in" on Jennings ahead of the trade deadline.

If Jennings can bring backfield depth or draft capital that can be used to find it, Minnesota might be convinced to make a deal. Jennings, who had 643 yards and nine touchdowns last season, would be worth it to a receiver-needy team.

Potential Suitors: New England Patriots, San Francisco 49ers

Projected Trade Value: 2027 5th-Round Pick

The Indianapolis Colts are barreling toward a rebuild. They recently fired general manager Chris Ballard. On Tuesday they traded away not one, but two high-profile players.

The Colts first agreed to send standout guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Later in the afternoon, they dealt defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick.

It's unlikely that interim GM Ed Dodds is finished making moves.

Wide receiver Josh Downs would be a logical trade candidate if Indy is willing to keep parting out its roster. He has 26 catches for 307 yards this season, and he could help a contender in need of receiver depth.

However, Downs is set to be a free agent in 2027 and may not be in Indianapolis' long-term plans after it gave Alec Pierce a four-year, $114 million extension in the offseason.

Potential Suitors: Kansas City Chiefs, Pittsburgh Steelers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 4th-Round Pick

There was some trade chatter involving Arizona Cardinals edge-rusher Josh Sweat during the offseason, but general manager Monti Ossenfort dismissed the idea of trading him at the time.

Of course, that was before Arizona started playing meaningful games and losing more often than not.

The Cardinals have earned a pair of upset wins in 2026, but they fell to 2-5 with Sunday's blowout loss to the Denver Broncos.

Sweat is a very logical trade chip for a team that may be looking to chase a quarterback in the 2027 draft. He has 16 tackles, two sacks, and seven quarterback pressures this season and can boost another team's pass-rushing rotation. However, he'll turn 30 in the spring and probably isn't a long-term fit for the rebuilding Cardinals.

While Sweat is signed through 2028, the Cardinals can release him with a post-June 1 designation in the spring and save $18.1 million in 2027 cap space.

Potential Suitors: Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers

Projected Trade Value: 2027 3rd-Round Pick

Philadelphia Eagles general manager Howie Roseman has traditionally been a buyer at the trade deadline. However, the Eagles face a very different situation this season than they've faced in the past.

Philly fell to 2-5 on Monday night, has lost quarterback Jalen Hurts for the season , and has a host of injuries at other key positions. At this point, it's becoming difficult to believe that the Eagles can get back in the NFC East race.

Roseman has already dealt center Cam Jurgens, and if the Eagles do believe their season is done, more moves could be on the horizon. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo would be a valuable trade chip if this is the case.

Ojomo left Monday night's game with an apparent injury, so his status will bear watching. However, he would be a very appealing target for most teams.

The 25-year-old has 18 tackles, two tackles for loss, and nine quarterback pressures this season as a rotational player. He's set to be a free agent in 2027, and the Eagles appear unlikely to re-sign him after extending both Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter this past offseason.

Potential Suitors: Carolina Panthers, Jacksonville Jaguars

4. Jonathan Taylor, RB, Indianapolis Colts

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 2nd-Round Pick

Schefter said on The Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday (beginning at the 1:24:18 mark) that his "understanding" is that Colts ownership doesn't want to trade star running back Jonathan Taylor.

However, the trades of both Nelson and Buckner would seem to signal that Indianapolis is open for business.

Taylor won't come cheaply. He remains one of the league's top dual-threat running backs, and he's an excellent support piece for the Colts' quarterback—whether they stick with Daniel Jones beyond this season or not. Additionally, moving Taylor will cost the Colts $10 million in dead cap next season.

Taylor might be viewed by some teams as a short-term option because, while this year's $7 million base salary is reasonable, that figure will jump to $15 million next year.

Still, Taylor is a legitimate difference-maker, and he could potentially put a team that is in the playoff conversation into the Super Bowl picture.

Potential Suitors: Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants

3. Landon Dickerson, G, Philadelphia Eagles

Schefter reported earlier this month that guard Landon Dickerson is a player that teams will be eyeing if the Eagles do decide to be deadline sellers.

"It would not surprise those in the league if teams start calling on Eagles guard Landon Dickerson when he is healthy enough to return from injured reserve," Schefter wrote on October 11.

Dickerson was on injured reserve with a knee injury, but he returned in Week 7 and appeared to be healthy. He played 100 percent of the offensive snaps in Monday's loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

A three-time Pro Bowler who is still only 28 years old, Dickerson would bring a strong return to Philadelphia.

Roseman won't want to completely tear down this Eagles roster. After seeing the Colts get third- and fifth-round picks for the 30-year-old Nelson, however, he could decide that now is the time to flip Dickerson for future draft capital.

2. Brian Thomas Jr., WR, Jacksonville Jaguars

Projected Trade Value: 2027 2nd- and 6th-Round Picks

The Jacksonville Jaguars continue to publicly assert their belief in third-year wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr., even though he has slipped down their offensive pecking order and was effectively benched for the second half of their last game.

"He's gonna be able to help us make plays this week," head coach Liam Coen told reporters on Monday. "I bet it, I know it. We're gonna continue to support him, throw our arm around him and continue to do what we gotta do to make plays on Sunday."

While Jacksonville may be publicly backing Thomas, though, it can't ignore the fact that now is a prime opportunity to get something in return for a player who may never get a second contract with the team. Some around the league also seem to believe that the Jags' public stance is a bit disingenuous.

"There are a lot of people around the league who believe Thomas could have a new home by the trade deadline," ESPN's Dan Graziano wrote last week.

Thomas was a big-play Pro Bowl receiver as a rookie, and he should interest top-tier contenders in need of receiving help.

Potential Suitors: Kansas City Chiefs, San Francisco 49ers

1. Khalil Mack, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers

Even with the league's worst record, Los Angeles has yet to enter sell-off mode. According to Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Chargers "insist they are trying to win games" and have given "no indication" that they're willing to deal.

At some point, though, the Chargers have to face the reality that they're not going to salvage their season. They should reach that conclusion before November 10, and once they do, trading Khalil Mack should be their top priority.

Mack is still a terrific pass-rusher. He has started all six games this season and has recorded 19 tackles, three sacks, five tackles for loss, and 11 quarterback pressures. He can help L.A. win games this season. However, he's playing on a one-year deal and probably won't be around beyond 2026.

Given how quickly things have spiraled out of control this season, why would Mack want to be back in Los Angeles?

According to the collective bargaining agreement —specifically, Appendix V, Paragraph 4—the Chargers could receive no higher than a fifth-round compensatory pick if Mack departed as a qualifying free agent, because he has at least 10 accrued seasons.

Anything more than a late fifth-round pick might be enough to pry Mack out of Los Angeles.

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, San Francisco 49ers

articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys capped Week 7 with a decisive win over a Philadelphia Eagles team that is ravaged by injuries. At this point in the 2026 season, many fantasy managers can probably relate to Philadelphia.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys capped Week 7 with a decisive win over a Philadelphia Eagles team that is ravaged by injuries. At this point in the 2026 season, many fantasy managers can probably relate to Philadelphia.

Just as the Eagles had to rely on backups like Tanner McKee, Dameon Pierce, and Marquise Brown, many managers will rely on deep sleepers and late waiver-wire additions in Week 8.

Here, you'll find a look at some of the top sleeper options who may still be available on the wire, their individual matchups, and some projections based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Managers looking for a fill-in at quarterback should consider New York Jets signal-caller Geno Smith. While the Jets lost to the previously winless Miami Dolphins, Smith put up some respectable numbers.

Smith tossed a trio of touchdown passes and yielded 24.5 fantasy points, his second-highest total of the season. He'll have a chance to approach 20 points again in Week 8 when the Jets host the Las Vegas Raiders.

The Raiders' defense has been worse against the run than against the pass. However, it hasn't been particularly good in any aspect and ranks 29th in both yards and points allowed. Through Week 7, it has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks.

Smith is rostered in 19 percent of fantasy leagues.

Week 8 Projection: 282 passing yards, 3 TDs, 1 INT, 12 rushing yards

Though he's going to remain part of a backfield rotation that also includes J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, Denver Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman is a veritable must-add this week. The Washington product logged 11 touches for 69 yards in Week 7 and helped spark Denver's sluggish running attack.

Head coach Sean Payton insinuated after the game that Coleman's role is likely to grow from here.

"He looked really good. Got to get him more touches," Payton said, per Susanna Weir of the team's official website.

Denver will face the Kansas City Chiefs, who have surrendered the eighth-fewest fantasy points to opposing running backs this season. However, Kansas City also allowed Emanuel Wilson to hit 100 yards on Sunday, which should give Denver the confidence needed to attack the Chiefs on the ground.

Coleman is rostered in just 35 percent of fantasy leagues.

Week 8 Projection: 51 rushing yards, 3 receptions, 29 receiving yards.

Baltimore Ravens rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane recorded just 25 yards on three catches during Sunday's blowout loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. However, it's worth noting that nothing really went right for Tyler Huntley and Baltimore's passing attack.

There's a very real chance that the Ravens will have Lamar Jackson back to face the Buffalo Bills in Week 8.

"I think he'll be in a decent spot, but we'll know a lot more on Wednesday," coach Jesse Minter said, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley .

Jackson's return should boost Lane's stock, as should a favorable matchup with Buffalo. The Bills have surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers this season.

Lane is rostered in 26 percent of fantasy leagues.

Week 8 Projection: 5 receptions, 67 yards

Minnesota Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson was a popular add last week, ahead of a favorable matchup with the Indianapolis Colts. He delivered 13.5 fantasy points and could reward managers with a similar outing in Week 8.

Despite Hockenson's popularity last week, he's still rostered in just 54 percent of leagues.

Hockenson is a strong start this week against a Detroit Lions defense that has been terrible against opposing tight ends. No team has surrendered more fantasy points to the position this season, and the margin is wide.

The Lions have surrendered an average of 24.7 fantasy points to tight ends, while the Washington Commanders are the next closest team, allowing 18.8.

Week 8 Projection: 6 receptions, 69 yards, 1 TD

articles.body:
The end of October is in sight, and Sunday's slate of NFL games will be the first to be played in November. While harsh winter conditions may still be a few weeks off, weather will become more of a factor in the foreseeable future.

As if the NFL needed more unpredictability in 2026.

It's been a wild season thus far, and it's still difficult to tell which teams are truly contenders and which are legitimately bad. The Minnesota Vikings are the last undefeated team, while the Los Angeles Chargers are the league's last winless squad—which exactly no one predicted at the start of the season.

Even weekly projections have become difficult, though that won't stop us from trying.

Here, we'll take an early look at the Week 8 slate, the latest odds, and the most accurate forecast information from The Weather Channel to make a few predictions.

Carolina Panthers (+3.5) at Green Bay Packers

Baltimore Ravens (+3.5) at Buffalo Bills

Tennessee Titans (+10.5) at Cincinnati Bengals

Arizona Cardinals (+6.5) at Dallas Cowboys (Retractable Roof)

Minnesota Vikings (+3.5) at Detroit Lions (Dome)

Indianapolis Colts (+8.5) at Jacksonville Jaguars

Forecast: Thunderstorms, Winds up to 15MPH, High of 77°F

Las Vegas Raiders (+1.5) at New York Jets

Cleveland Browns (+3.5) at Pittsburgh Steelers

Atlanta Falcons (+2.5) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams (Dome)

Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos

New England Patriots (-7.5) at Miami Dolphins

Philadelphia Eagles (+5.5) at Washington Commanders

Byes: Houston Texans, New Orleans Saints, New York Giants, San Francisco 49ers

Week 8 will begin with an intriguing matchup between the Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers. Both NFC contenders are coming off of disappointing losses, but Carolina is coming off a loss of the blowout variety.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fully exploited Carolina's league-worst run defense, and the Packers will undoubtedly try to do the same. The recent return of Josh Jacobs just might allow them to do it.

Sunday's afternoon slate will feature several matchups between playoff contenders. The Cleveland Browns' game against the Pittsburgh Steelers will determine the top spot in the AFC North, while the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will vie for the top spot in the AFC West.

The Baltimore Ravens will have a pivotal game against the Buffalo Bills, though they may have starting quarterback Lamar Jackson back to face Josh Allen and Co.

"I think he was able to get in a little bit of work obviously towards the end of last week," Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley . "I think he'll be in a decent spot, but we'll know a lot more on Wednesday."

The Atlanta Falcons will visit the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a game that will mean plenty in the wide-open NFC South. That's one of two Florida games that could be heavily impacted by weather on Sunday.

The week's action will be capped by a Monday night matchup that could be an NFC Championship preview.

The Chicago Bears' offense has been rolling with Caleb Williams back in the lineup, and their defense is starting to come together. However, the Seattle Seahawks just flexed their elite defense this past Sunday, and a revitalized running game could be enough to get Seattle another win.

Zach Charbonnet has been designated to return from last year's ACL tear, and rookie Jadarian Price (chest) will return to practice this week. There's no guarantee that either will suit up against Chicago, but head coach Mike Macdonald did tell reporters that one or both could return.

Oh, and the Seahawks just acquired standout guard Quenton Nelson in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts.

articles.title: Ranking the Best 5 Buffalo Bills Teams of All Time
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills exit their bye week as the betting favorites to win Super Bowl LXI.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills exit their bye week as the betting favorites to win Super Bowl LXI.

With Buffalo still seeking its first Lombardi Trophy, this 2026 squad has a chance to establish itself as the greatest team in franchise history.

As the post-bye push begins, let's look back and rank the five greatest teams in Bills history.

The Snapshot: This team is representing the 2020s, as I could have just as easily made the case for a 13-3 2020 team that was even more dominant offensively and went to the AFC Championship, a 13-3 2022 team that matched that squad with a franchise-best 6.13 yards per play and sent eight guys to the Pro Bowl, or even an 11-6 2021 team that still boasts the highest average margin of victory in team history. These Bills went 13-4 in Josh Allen's lone MVP season, coming closer to the Super Bowl than any other squad from this era.

Key Stat: An NFL-best plus-24 turnover differential (32 takeaways to just eight giveaways). The offense tied the all-time NFL record for the fewest turnovers in a single season (six interceptions, two lost fumbles).

The Case for Greatness: Allen was sensational from wire to wire en route to MVP honors, pushing the Chiefs to the brink in an unforgettable 32-29 AFC title game duel at Arrowhead.

The Case Against: Sean McDermott's defense relied heavily on takeaways rather than down-to-down dominance. When the turnover faucet dried up, they struggled against elite quarterbacks and finished outside the top 10 in scoring defense.

The Snapshot: The Lou Saban-coached Bills repeated as champions in 1965, finishing 10-3-1 with quarterback Jack Kemp winning AFL MVP and Saban earning Coach of the Year honors.

Key Stat: This remains the most recent champion in professional football to shut out its opponent in the championship game, with Buffalo smashing the Chargers 23-0 to capture the title.

The Case for Greatness: Buffalo sent seven players to the AFL All-Star Game, while four earned first-team All-AFL honors to anchor the league's No. 1 scoring defense.

The Case Against: In an eight-team league, Buffalo's offense ranked just third in scoring, suffered a midseason slump, and stumbled to three losses and a tie during the regular season.

The Snapshot: The first champion in franchise history led the league both offensively and defensively in a dominant campaign from start to finish.

Key Stat: Their .857 winning percentage stemming from a 12-2 regular-season record remains the highest in franchise history.

The Case for Greatness: These Bills outscored opponents by an average of 11.3 points per game before beating the Chargers 20-7 in the AFL Championship game. And they placed 10 players in the AFL All-Star Game, including six first-team All-AFL selections.

The Case Against: As with the 1965 squad, this team predates the AFL-NFL merger in an eight-team league.

The Snapshot: This 13-3 juggernaut featured eight Pro Bowlers, three first-team All-Pros and five future Hall of Famers in a Super Bowl campaign.

Key Stat: The Jim Kelly-led offense averaged 5.92 yards per play, which was the best in team history until the Josh Allen era.

The Case for Greatness: Thurman Thomas was league MVP and Offensive Player of the Year as Buffalo's offense produced its most prolific yardage season to that point in franchise history. The Bills scored 24 points in their Super Bowl XXVI loss to a historically dominant Washington team.

The Case Against: While the K-Gun reached its peak this season, the defense declined significantly from 1990 and actually became somewhat of a liability. They were also much less competitive in the Super Bowl than they were in '90.

The Snapshot: The most complete Bills team in modern league history fell one 47-yard field goal short of winning the Super Bowl following a 13-3 regular season.

Key Stat: They not only led the NFL in scoring, but these Bills put up 95 points in their two AFC playoff games before falling 20-19 to the Giants in Super Bowl XXV.

The Case for Greatness: This team had 10 Pro Bowlers, compared to eight in 1991. It came the closest the franchise has ever come to winning a Lombardi, thanks to a historic offense and a stout D led by Defensive Player of the Year Bruce Smith.

The Case Against: The 1964 and 1965 teams were league champions, while this team fell short.

The 2026 Verdict: Can This Team Crash the Top Five?

Of course the answer is yes. Despite significant defensive struggles, Buffalo's offense has been so dominant over a 5-1 start that the Bills remain on track for the AFC's No. 1 seed.

The Bills could easily end up with the MVP in Allen, and at least a few All-Pros among Allen, James Cook, Greg Rousseau, and Deone Walker. The defense has a top-10 ceiling based on talent, and the offense is operating at a historic pace with 32.8 points per game thus far.

If these Bills can continue on the current trajectory and win 14-plus games before making a run to the Super Bowl, they may be the best version of the team in history. If they win that game, it's a no-brainer. But if they fall short of a Super Bowl appearance yet again, we'll likely just be weighing this team against the 2024, 2022, 2021 and 2020 squads for the No. 5 spot on this list next year.

articles.title: Behind the NFL stardom, Aaron Rodgers has taken a different path: How his private life and career decisions shaped his public image
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers is back with the Steelers on a one-year deal for 2026, and he has confirmed it will be his last NFL season. He is 42 and a four-time MVP.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers is back with the Steelers on a one-year deal for 2026, and he has confirmed it will be his last NFL season. He is 42 and a four-time MVP. Away from the field, he has spent two years guarding his personal life. He secretly married a woman named Brittani in 2025, and he shares almost nothing about her. Those choices now shape how fans read him, as much as the stats do.Aaron Rodgers keeps his marriage private by choiceAaron Rodgers did not announce his wife. He mentioned "girlfriend Brittani" on The Pat McAfee Show in December 2024, and the public learned of the marriage later. Since then, he has said she has no social media and wants to stay a private person.That has not stopped the questions. He has not been seen with her in public, and some reports questioned whether the marriage legally took place. Rodgers pushed back hard on the McAfee show in June 2025. He called the demand for details embarrassing and said, "my private life is staying private." At Steelers camp he went further and described a "sick society."Notice what he is doing here. He chose public life for the job. He is refusing to extend it to his home. Some fans find that fair. Others hear a man who spent years in headlines and now wants the door shut.His wife had a say in the retirement callThe retirement question hung over Pittsburgh for months. Rodgers has said his wife was part of the answer. He told reporters he had many conversations with her, and that after the draft he decided he wanted to come back.It is a small detail, but it tells you something. The same man who dodges every question about her credits her with the biggest decision of his late career. He gives out one fact and nothing around it.Mike Tomlin's exit and McCarthy's arrival changed his plansThe football side was just as slow and uncertain. Rodgers had said he signed with Pittsburgh in 2025 largely because of Mike Tomlin, so Tomlin's departure left his return in doubt. He admitted he figured Tomlin's exit meant the end for him too.Then the Steelers hired Mike McCarthy. McCarthy coached Rodgers in Green Bay from 2006 to 2018, and the pair won Super Bowl XLV together. That changed the math. Rodgers said that once the hire was made, he began opening his mind to coming back. The reunion gave him a coach he trusts and a reason to stay.This is a pattern. He kept the Steelers waiting through the offseason for a second straight year. Last year he did not commit until mandatory minicamp in June. Teams build plans around a quarterback. Rodgers makes them wait.The cost is real. Pittsburgh drafted Penn State's Drew Allar in the third round as a hedge. The production has held up, too. In 2025 he threw for 3,322 yards, 24 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He also led the team to an AFC North title. That is hard to argue with.When asked if this was the end, he answered, "Yes. This is it." No hedge this time.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Puka Nacua’s mother Penina raised six children after tragedy struck in 2012 - Inside the Los Angeles Rams star’s family and football journey
articles.summary: Puka Nacua’s quick rise to NFL stardom is more than a story of talent and determination; it is a heartfelt tribute to the loving family that shaped him.
articles.body: Puka Nacua’s quick rise to NFL stardom is more than a story of talent and determination; it is a heartfelt tribute to the loving family that shaped him. His late father, Lionel Nacua, ignited his passion for football, while his mother, Penina Nacua, became his strong pillar of strength after tragedy struck.Lionel Nacua’s deep love for football inspired his five sons to chase the sport, laying the perfect groundwork for their athletic pursuits. And through sacrifice, resilience, and unfaltering love, Penina Nacua helped keep Puka’s dreams alive while raising six children.As the Los Angeles Rams wide receiver continues to make his irrevocable mark, he carries his family’s dedication onto the gridiron. Every achievement is deeply personal, and he credits his parents and grandmother for their unwavering support and love.Who are Puka Nacua’s parentsPuka Nacua’s parents are Penina and the late Lionel Nacua. They brought together Samoan and Hawaiian roots that shaped a family built on respect, unity, and resilience.As per Pro Football Network, Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver is of Polynesian descent.He grew up in Utah but his heritage traces back to Samoa. He also has Portuguese and Native Hawaiian roots.Lionel Nacua’s dream inspired all five sons’ football careersLionel Nacua wrestled and was a huge football fan. From an early age, Lionel immersed his children in football, encouraging sibling rivalries to toughen them for the game’s growing demands.“My husband loved defense,” Penina Nacua said in 2023. “He would have everybody suiting up and putting on the shoulder pads, and he’d make them go head-on, one-on-one.”“His [Lionel] passions for his sons playing football was like above and beyond,” Penina said in 2024. “He loved football and I remember him just being in love with his sons because they had this Samoan build, you know. Just seeing them, he was like, ’My boys are gonna be athletes.’”Lionel’s dream was for all five of his sons to play football, and today, each has followed that path: Kai excelled as a defensive back at BYU and played in both the NFL and UFL;Isaiah played defensive line at BYU and served a church mission; Samson starred as a wide receiver at Utah and BYU before playing professionally; Puka shined at Washington and BYU before joining the NFL’s Los Angeles Rams; and Tei is carrying on the legacy as a wide receiver committed to BYU.Puka absorbed lessons from watching football footage and seasoned players, developing a love for the sport long before he turned pro. When Lionel passed away from diabetes complications in 2012, Puka was just 11 years old.Though his father’s absence left a void, the wisdom and drive Lionel instilled remain at the heart of the family. Inspired by his father’s battle, Puka now champions diabetes awareness through the league’s My Cause My Cleats initiative.Penina Nacua raised six children after tragedyAfter Lionel Nacua’s passing in 2012, Penina Nacua faced the daunting task of raising six children on her own. She juggled their education and athletic dreams, meeting every challenge with unfaltering strength.Puka often credits his mother’s resilience and devotion, cherishing the special bond that has guided him through every step of his football journey. “When I was younger, my mom had to be the strength for us when my father passed away,” Puka said via Deseret News in 2024.“There was never a moment where we couldn’t rely on my mom being there for us.”“My mother is everything to me and my family,” Puka said in 2024. “Being able to be the rock of our family and support us in that hard time. The strength of the single mother, being able to carry all of us kids and then to continue to carry on, it’s something that I used to call upon.”"The strength to continue to push on,” Puka said in 2023. “And to be there in all the significant moments for me, and especially for my siblings, being the younger one, of watching her find a way to go to practice over here, go to practice over there, be at this game, and to be a team mom, and all those things.The things that she sacrificed and the strength that that requires is something that I hold dear to my heart.”Puka Nacua’s siblings and grandmother inspired his football careerPuka Nacua grew up alongside five siblings - four brothers, Kai, Samson, Isaiah, and Tei, and a sister, Chanel - in a household where football was a family tradition. The brothers’ shared passion for the sport fostered a competitive spirit that sharpened Puka’s skills and drive.He attended Orem High School in Utah. Then played college football at Washington before transferring to BYU to be closer to his grandmother, Fa’atamali’i Saole, after her ovarian cancer diagnosis. Even his brother, Samson, left his beloved Utah Utes for BYU.“Coming back to be home with family for sure,” Samson said in 2021. “Grandma was sick. Mom was going through a lot trying to help grandma. Me and Puka were talking, and I was like, ‘D*ng, bro, we hadn’t played with each other in a long time, since pe*-w*e football.’ So it was perfect timing for everything.”“My dad, it kind of started with him,” Puka said in 2021. “Him having the idea that all of us brothers being able to play at the same school. It started with Kai coming here to BYU.But then my grandma, my mom’s mom, she used to come to my games in high school. But she was never a fan of going outside the house. But she said if we were to come play at BYU, she would be there every game.So, when she said that, we were like, ‘Okay, we’ll be there.’ We’ve always got to listen to mama. And then if mom’s mom says something, there is no hesitating there.”As Puka shattered NFL rookie records in Week 18 vs. the San Francisco 49ers during the 2023 NFL season, he sensed his late father and grandmother beside him, their presence woven into every moment.“Him and my grandma, I know they were up there. I hope they get to watch every game. But they were out there enjoying this one with me because there was a peace and calmness throughout the game that I was able to feel that was different from other ones.And I know they were out there with me. So, it was sweet,” said Puka.Puka Nacua and his grandmother shared a special bondPuka’s grandmother immigrated to the U.S. from West Samoa [the name of Samoa until 1997] with her only daughter Penina, as per The Salt Lake Tribune.Puka and his mother Penina share heartfelt memories of Puka’s grandmother and the special bond they shared. His mother revealed that Puka’s nickname came from his chubby appearance as a baby.“My mother named ‘Puka’ as a nickname for him because when he was six, nine months old, he was a chubby little version of my husband,” said Penina.“My legal government name is Makea Manu Nacua and in Samoan, the name ‘Puka’ means chubby,” said Puka.The family also recalled Puka’s grandmother’s warmth, affection, and deep connection to others. She made everyone feel loved and valued throughout her life. “Her and Puka just had a close relationship. Puka was just kind of like her baby,” said Penina.“The grandmother-grandson relationship was one that started from a very young age. I know my mom has a lot of baby pictures and the person in a lot of those baby photos was my grandma,” Puka said.“The connection that my grandma not only had with me and how important and special she made me feel, but then also the time that she would take to interact with the people that she came across.And I think everybody who knows her definitely felt that connection and that love and maybe sometimes a little aggressive sometimes, but in the best way.”Puka Nacua’s football journey from BYU to NFL stardom2018 - Earned Utah Gatorade Player of the Year honors at Orem High School after a record-breaking senior season with 103 receptions, 2,336 receiving yards and 26 touchdowns.2019 to 2020 - Played college football at the University of Washington [Washington Huskies]. He recorded 16 receptions for 319 yards and 3 touchdowns.2021 to 2022 - Transferred to BYU. He finished his college career with 91 catches, 1,430 receiving yards, and 11 touchdowns.2023 - The Los Angeles Rams selected him in the fifth round of the NFL Draft as their 177th overall pick. He set NFL rookie records with 105 receptions and 1,486 receiving yards. He won his first Pro Bowl. He earned a spot on PFWA All-Rookie Team.2024 - Recorded 79 receptions for 990 yards and 3 touchdowns even while missing games due to knee injuries.2025 - Posted a career-best 129 receptions for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns. He established himself as one of the Los Angeles Rams’ leading offensive players. He earned NFL receptions leader honors. He won his second Pro Bowl.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
