articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Potential Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs Trades After Colts' Nelson, Buckner Deals
articles.summary: Running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs have emerged as names that could be on the trade block amid the Indianapolis Colts' on-the-fly rebuild.
articles.body:
Running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs have emerged as names that could be on the trade block amid the Indianapolis Colts' on-the-fly rebuild.

On the heels of the 2-5 Colts dealing guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers on Tuesday, there is some belief that they may not be done selling off pieces.

The biggest trade asset remaining on Indy's roster is Taylor, although there is reportedly some doubt over whether interim general manager Ed Dodds would be willing to move him.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , opposing teams "aren't totally sold" on the Colts trading Taylor "despite heavy interest." He added that Taylor "isn't a slam dunk" to get moved.

The Colts signed Taylor to a two-year, $44 million contract extension in August, meaning he is under contract through 2028.

ESPN's Dan Graziano noted that Taylor's contract is "tradeable" since the acquiring team would only have to take on $8 million in prorated salary plus bonus money for this season, and could technically move on from Taylor within five days after the Super Bowl without having to make any financial commitment for next season.

While the Colts do appear to be in the midst of a fire sale, it is fair to wonder if they would trade Taylor since he is the face of the franchise, signed for multiple years and the centerpiece of the offense, having eclipsed 1,400 rushing yards in each of the past two seasons.

As for Downs, he is set to become a free agent during the offseason, perhaps making him more attainable.

Per Fowler, Downs "has emerged as a hot name this week" since multiple teams with a need at wide receiver have "shown interest" in him.

Fowler added that he senses Downs "would not be against a change of scenery," although he isn't sure if the Colts will move them since they are already thin at wide receiver with Alec Pierce on injured reserve.

A third-round pick by the Colts in the 2023 NFL draft, Downs set career highs in 2024 with 72 receptions for 803 yards and five touchdowns, but his production dipped last season to 58 grabs for 566 yards and four touchdowns.

He is on pace for a career-worst season in 2026, recording 26 catches for 307 yards and no touchdowns through seven games.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Brian Thomas Jr., Chances of Jaguars Dealing WR Before 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: Now that trade deadline season is in full swing after the Indianapolis Colts' moves on Tuesday, another AFC South team appears poised to make a significant deal within the next two weeks.
articles.body:
Now that trade deadline season is in full swing after the Indianapolis Colts' moves on Tuesday, another AFC South team appears poised to make a significant deal within the next two weeks.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the feeling among multiple executives around the NFL is that Brian Thomas Jr.'s days with the Jacksonville Jaguars "are numbered" as his role in the offense has significantly diminished this season.

In the same article, Dan Graziano noted several teams still consider Thomas to be a "high-end talent" and would trade "something of value" to bring him in.

Fowler did add it's not considered a "slam dunk" that Thomas will get moved, but a fresh start could serve the third-year wideout well.

The Jaguars are in a tricky spot because they would seemingly not want to trade Thomas within the AFC given that they are a strong playoff contender and don't want the risk of him potentially helping a team they could go up against in January.

Teams like the Kansas City Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers have been cited as potentially searching for receiver help leading up to the trade deadline.

Another potential hurdle could be the cost if the Jaguars are using the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade as a comparison. The Arizona Cardinals were able to get a 2027 second-round draft pick from the Houston Texans for Harrison.

It's not an unfair comparison since both players recently turned 24 and were first-round picks in the 2024 draft. Thomas' ceiling in the NFL is much higher than Harrison's since he put up 1,282 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie.

So far this season, it does seem like Thomas isn't a factor in Jacksonville's offensive game plan. He has nine catches in six games, has played fewer than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in three of those contests, including a total of 15 snaps in Week 6 against the Texans.

This does feel like the last opportunity for the Jaguars to get any significant value for Thomas. An acquiring team would be getting him at a time when they can evaluate his play with his fifth-year option needing to be decided on in the offseason.

The NFL trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 10. Jacksonville has two games in a four-day span starting on Sunday against the Colts before a Week 9 Thursday night matchup against the Baltimore Ravens on Nov. 5.

articles.title: Justin Tucker, Chiefs Reportedly Agree to Contract Amid Harrison Butker's Struggles
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are reportedly bringing in veteran competition for struggling kicker Harrison Butker.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs are reportedly bringing in veteran competition for struggling kicker Harrison Butker.

According to Sam McDowell of the Kansas City Star and Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, the Chiefs are signing veteran kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad.

The move comes amid Butker converting just 11 of his 16 field goal attempts (68.8 percent) through six games this season.

Tucker, 36, spent 13 seasons with the Baltimore Ravens from 2012 to 2024, establishing himself as one of the most successful kickers in NFL history during that time.

A seven-time Pro Bowler, five-time First Team All-Pro, one-time Super Bowl champion and member of the Pro Football Hall of Fame's All-Decade Team for the 2010s, Tucker was a consistent performer for most of his tenure in Baltimore.

Among qualified players, he is the second-most-accurate kicker in NFL history, making 89.1 percent of his field goal attempts.

Tucker also ranks 14th in NFL history in total field goals made (417) and 17th in career points scored (1,775).

However, Tucker had the worst season of his career in 2024, which was when he kicked most recently in an NFL regular-season contest.

Tucker made a career-low 73.3 percent of his field goals that season, going 22-for-30. He also missed two of his 62 extra-point tries.

While Tucker has participated in tryouts and workouts with the New Orleans Saints, Indianapolis Colts and New York Jets since 2024, joining the Chiefs' practice squad marks the first time he has officially joined a new team since departing Baltimore.

Like Tucker, Butker has long been considered one of the top kickers of his generation, winning three Super Bowls during his 10-year run in Kansas City.

Butker is also among the most-accurate kickers in NFL history, ranking fifth on the all-time list with a field goal percentage of 87.3 percent.

He is trending toward performing below his career field goal percentage for the fourth time in the past five seasons, though, and his five missed field goals this season already match the amount he had all of last season.

Butker had an especially tough time during a 20-3 road loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday night, missing two of his three field goal attempts.

Signing Tucker to the practice squad is not a guarantee that Butker will lose his job, but if the misses continue to pile up, the Chiefs now have an experienced secondary option they can turn to.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Titans' Tony Pollard Amid Jonathan Taylor Buzz at 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: Amid the focus on marquee names such as Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley as potential trade candidates, Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard could be most prominent player at the position to get moved before Nov. 10.
articles.body:
Amid the focus on marquee names such as Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley as potential trade candidates, Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard could be most prominent player at the position to get moved before Nov. 10.

Per ESPN's Dan Graziano , Pollard is considered "more likely" to be traded than someone like Taylor.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler wrote in a separate report that Pollard is viewed as an "attractive fallback plan" if the Colts decide to hold on to Taylor.

Fowler did quote one AFC executive who was skeptical of the Titans moving Pollard because they don't think the team wants to "take weapons away" from Cam Ward right now.

One reason a Pollard deal would seem more likely than Taylor getting traded is contractual. Pollard is in the final season of his three-year, $21.8 million contract with Tennessee.

Taylor just signed a two-year, $44 million extension with the Indianapolis Colts in August. His 2027 salary of $16 million doesn't become fully guaranteed until February 19, so in theory a team could decide to move on from him without any long-term financial commitment.

However, given the Colts' reported asking price for Taylor is at least a second-round draft pick, an acquiring team would seem unlikely to give up that much for a rental back.

Pollard has been a bright spot in what has otherwise been a disappointing Titans offense. The 29-year-old ranks 10th in the NFL with 478 rushing yards and is tied for 11th with four rushing touchdowns.

He is also a reliable receiver out of the backfield with at least 30 catches in each of the past five seasons.

Given Pollard's age and contract status, it wouldn't seem to make much sense for the Titans to prioritize keeping him if they can get a decent mid-round draft pick back.

articles.title: NFL Exec Links Cowboys to Josh Sweat Trade at 2026 Deadline, 'Makes a Lot of Sense'
articles.summary: Some NFL teams are expecting the Arizona Cardinals to follow up their trade of Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans by parting ways with edge rusher Josh Sweat, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday.
articles.body:
Some NFL teams are expecting the Arizona Cardinals to follow up their trade of Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans by parting ways with edge rusher Josh Sweat, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday.

According to Fowler, "rival teams could see [Sweat] getting moved" ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

One NFC executive told Fowler: "Sweat to Dallas makes a lot of sense to me. That's a profile fit."

Fowler noted there are rumors 29-year-old Sweat wants an extension despite already being signed through 2028, which "could complicate" a potential trade. He still named the Cowboys as well as the Chicago Bears and San Francisco 49ers as potential "team fits" for Sweat.

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said in a Tuesday appearance on 105.3 The Fan he felt it was "unlikely" the Cowboys' defense would get the opportunity to add a player from outside the organization this season, per DallasCowboys.com's Tommy Yarrish .

"But if it's there, I'll do it," Jones added, per Yarrish.

Discussion of the Cowboys' edge depth is taking place after the organization traded a 2027 fourth-round draft pick to the Green Bay Packers in order to acquire Rashan Gary over the offseason.

Cowboys just improved to 3-4 and upped their chances of winning the NFC East with a Monday night win over the Eagles, but Gary and the Dallas pass rush once more struggled to put pressure on a Philadelphia offense that recorded 200 yards through the air.

Sweat, who is in the second year of his four-year, $76.4 million deal with the Cardinals, has recorded two sacks, 16 tackles (three for loss) and four quarterback hits in seven games this season.

He has added 12 pressures, 10 stops and eight hurries, according to PFF , but popped up on the Cardinals injury report earlier this fall after undergoing an undisclosed procedure this offseason.

Sweat's health, the Cardinals' asking price and the Cowboys' willingness to further chip away at their limited 2027 draft stock in a push to win an injury-weakened division could determine how seriously Jones considers a potential trade.

Jones will get his next look at Sweat this Sunday, when the Cardinals (2-5) arrive in Dallas for a 1 p.m. ET Week 8 matchup.

articles.title: Chiefs reportedly sign Justin Tucker to practice squad after Harrison Butker misses two field goals in Week 7
articles.summary: Justin Tucker has not kicked in the NFL since 2024.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs could be on the verge of replacing longtime kicker Harrison Butker. Days after Butker missed two field goals in an embarrassing 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, the Chiefs reportedly signed kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad, per the Kansas City Star.

Tucker has not appeared in the NFL since the 2024 season. He was released by the Baltimore Ravens ahead of the 2025 NFL season after being accused of sexual misconduct by multiple massage therapists.

Tucker has received tryouts with other NFL teams in the years since his release, but has gone unsigned until now.

Prior to his release, Tucker was considered one of the best kickers in the NFL. From 2013 to 2023, he made the All-Pro first team five times and was a seven-time Pro Bowler.

His performance, however, started to slip in his final season with the Ravens. Tucker made a career-worst 73.3% of his field-goal attempts that year, with many of his misses coming from longer distances. Despite that, it looked as though the Ravens planned to bring Tucker back in 2025 until accusations against him came to light.

Tucker was ultimately handed a 10-game suspension from the NFL ahead of the 2025 season. Though he was not with a team, the NFL counted the first 10 weeks of the regular season as time served for Tucker. Because of that, he will be eligible to kick immediately if the Chiefs promote him to their active roster.

Prior to 2026, Butker had been a model of consistency on the field. The 31-year-old was coming off a nine-year stretch in which he made at least 84% of his field goals in every season.

But Butker has experienced some uncharacteristic misses to start 2026. In addition to his two missed field goals against the Seahawks, Butker has missed three other field-goal attempts so far, the majority of which have come from 50+ yards out, where Butker has made just 2-of-6 attempts this year.

articles.title: New Jets Rumors on Aaron Glenn's Hot Seat as HC After Loss to Dolphins, 2-5 Start to 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn isn't in imminent danger of losing his job with the team sitting at 2-5, according to ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler.
articles.body:
New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn isn't in imminent danger of losing his job with the team sitting at 2-5, according to ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler .

Graziano reported his sense is that Glenn will remain in the role for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season, after which ownership and the front office will make an evaluation.

Fowler wrote that "Glenn likely will get some time to attempt to right the ship, but the hot seat conversation is real."

The Jets are situated well with three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL draft. Few expected them to be a big winner this year, so from the outset, the season was about setting the table for the future.

According to Graziano, that's the basis on which Glenn will mostly be judged:

"What the Jets want to have established by the end of this season is at least a foundation of a winning culture and an environment in which a young quarterback would be in position to quickly thrive and be happy. It's hard to look at the Jets right now and think they're on either one of those tracks. There is time to turn it around, but if it keeps going the way it has so far, this is absolutely a situation we'll be watching for a potential change."

Fowler ended the conversation by saying it's unlikely the Jets would kick general manager Darren Mougey to the curb in the offseason since he has done well to build up their draft assets.

There are some encouraging signs from the team.

Braelon Allen has anchored the backfield with Breece Hall injured. He eclipsed the century mark for the second time in the 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins.

David Bailey is tied for fifth in the league in sacks with 5.5. Fellow rookies Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper Jr. have shown flashes.

But New York has yet to win a game within the division under Glenn. By now, fans have probably seen the stat about how badly the team is getting outscored in the final two minutes as well.

There's arguably more evidence in favor of firing Glenn than retaining him, but a coaching change wouldn't achieve much. The Jets aren't a playoff-caliber team, and whoever succeeds Glenn would be an interim replacement rather than a coach who may guide the team in 2027 and beyond.

Maybe the situation continues to devolve to a point where Glenn absolutely has to go. Otherwise, giving him the rest of the season might be the best call.

articles.title: Travis Kelce Sounds Off on 'Frustrating' Offensive Showing in Chiefs' Loss to Seahawks
articles.summary: Travis Kelce is frustrated with the effort a shorthanded Kansas City Chiefs offense put in against the Seattle Seahawks while conceding the team's first loss of the season last Sunday.
articles.body:
Travis Kelce is frustrated with the effort a shorthanded Kansas City Chiefs offense put in against the Seattle Seahawks while conceding the team's first loss of the season last Sunday.

The Chiefs went without a trip to the red zone for the first time in the Patrick Mahomes era in the 20-3 Week 6 road defeat.

"It felt like they were playing prevent the entire time. It just let the front four cause havoc in the run game and get out of the pocket... It was a pretty frustrating game from the jump," Kelce told his brother Jason Kelce around the 30:00 mark of Wednesday's New Heights podcast .

Kelce continued, "It's frustrating, because we were rolling as a unit for a while there. And I think we're not far off from getting right back to it... I think we just need to learn from this, feel how it felt to get our tail kicked like that, and never let it happen again."

Kelce pointed toward the turning point of the loss taking place when he was called for an illegal motion penalty on the first drive.

"We were rolling, that first drive, and that just kind of stalled us," Kelce said. "From there, it was just bad techniques, bad fundamentals, just okay effort."

The Chiefs were missing injured wide receivers Tyquan Thornton and Rashee Rice from the loss, during which Mahomes completed just 57.6 percent of his passes and threw an interception.

Eight players including Kelce made a catch last Sunday, but the group combined for just 165 receiving yards and no touchdowns.

Kelce said the Chiefs' receiving unit, which will still be missing at least Thornton for Week 7 amid his recovery from the significant ankle injury he suffered earlier this month, will need to focus on working together in order to give Mahomes more opportunities for success going forward.

"If it's the backside of a route, being ready and on time. If it's the called route that we're trying to get open, being on time, and being where you need to be... making the read easy for Pat to get the ball out on time so that the offensive line doesn't have to strain for more than what they typically do," Kelce said.

The Chiefs (5-1) are still heading into Week 7 in the top spot of the AFC West, but that could change based on this weekend's matchup against the Denver Broncos (5-2).

Whether Mahomes, Kelce and the rest of the Chiefs offense are able to rebound from their blowout defeat by Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET in Denver could play a role in which team makes it out of the division this winter.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor trade scenarios: 5 best landing spots and what each means for fantasy football
articles.summary: Scott Pianowski breaks down Jonathan Taylor's fantasy outlook with five potential trade partners.
articles.body:
Not long ago, an in-season trade speculation piece was basically a waste of time. NFL teams were reluctant to make deals, and when they actually occurred, it was rare for the players on the move to quickly acclimate to their new clubs. Much ado about nothing.

But things have shifted in recent years. It's helped that the trade deadline is now parked in November (it previously was slotted after Week 6). And teams seem less afraid of making mistakes now, more willing to take some chances.

This brings us to Jonathan Taylor, starting running back for the Colts. He's the center of the NFL rumor mill at the moment .

Indianapolis, of course, is off to a horrible start. The Colts sit 2-5 and even in a weak division, they're given just a 7% chance of making the playoffs, per DVOA.

The front office realizes the season is basically cooked, and Tuesday the Colts made a couple of trades. Star offensive guard Quenton Nelson was shipped to Seattle , and stalwart defensive tackle DeForest Buckner was reunited with the 49ers . The Colts landed a third and fifth-round pick for Nelson, and a fourth-round pick for Buckner. Taylor could be the next Colt to hit the trade market.

While fantasy managers paid keen attention to both deals, especially the Nelson move, a Taylor swap would be seismic in the fantasy landscape. Let's examine the prime contenders for a possible Taylor trade, and see how the pieces fit. (And while you're reading the shopping list, don't forger to add Seth McGowan, the Indianapolis backup RB, just in case.)

Here's a pretty clean fit. The undefeated Vikings are all defense (second in DVOA) and no offense (30th in DVOA) through their opening six games. Aaron Jones Sr. has been a decent back for a decade, but will be 32 in December. Jordan Mason isn't a bad player, but he's caught just 28 passes in his career (none this season). Taylor would immediately give the Vikings a three-down bell cow, and take some pressure off struggling QB Kyler Murray.

The Vikings likely recognize their window here. The NFC doesn't have a dominant team. The NFC East and NFC South between them might not have any good teams. The Rams have gotten off to a nightmare start. The 49ers are formidable, but battling cluster injuries. Seattle is a good but imperfect team. Even in a competitive NFC North, it's a good time for Minnesota to shove in some chips.

This would likely be a slight upgrade for Taylor. At least game flow would be improved more often than not.

Speaking of those imperfect Seahawks, maybe they could kick the tires on Taylor. They upgraded their running game with the Nelson move Tuesday, but the backfield is still a bunch of question marks. Emanuel Wilson is averaging just 3.6 yards per carry. Jadarian Price (chest) and Zach Charbonnet (torn ACL) recently had their practice windows opened, but they're far from guarantees. Seattle's team shape is much like Minnesota's — dominant defense, below-average offense. Taylor would instantly make the Seahawks more balanced and more dangerous.

Taylor's fantasy value would remain lofty in Seattle. This team often plays with a lead, and it seldom wants Sam Darnold to throw 40 or more passes. The offensive line now grades as a plus unit with Nelson aboard.

Here's yet another team with a defensive tilt. The Broncos are 5-2 on the strength of their No. 5 defense (per DVOA). The offense ranks just 30th in yards per game, though a difficult schedule has played into that (DVOA ranks Denver 16th on offense, which underlines how taxing the slate has been). The team is averaging just 3.8 yards per carry.

But maybe the timing for a Taylor trade isn't right here. Rookie Jonah Coleman was impressive in his Week 7 return (11 touches, 69 yards) and was a versatile back in his four-year college career. The Broncos also have veteran J.K. Dobbins and second-year back RJ Harvey, imperfect players but legitimate NFL runners. I suspect the Broncos would surely listen on a Taylor trade, but I doubt they'd do it proactively.

The Packers might have choked up when they saw how inexpensive Nelson was in trade. Green Bay's offensive line has been screaming for help all year as one of the worst run-blocking units in the league. But a Taylor trade might complicate things, given Josh Jacobs has returned.

Taylor managers don't want their back to head to Green Bay. The blocking will be worse, the competition for the ball will be increased. I suspect the Packers are just a longshot in the Taylor sweepstakes anyway, even as they've been one of the primary teams mentioned.

Here's the sleeper in the Taylor chase, a team that hasn't been among the common suitors discussed. Maybe that's an oversight. Cincinnati sits at 4-2, is second in the DVOA ranks, has assembled a plus offense and (for once) a credible defense. Keep Joe Burrow healthy and great things can happen.

The one disappointment in the Cincinnati offense (fantasy managers know all about it) has been Chase Brown. He's averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, and he's been nothing special as a receiver (4.3 yards per target). At his best, Brown is a solid player. Taylor at his best is a superstar. Maybe Cincinnati could get frisky in the Taylor market.

Fantasy managers would probably OK the move. If the Bengals moved for Taylor, it surely wouldn't be to make him a committee back. When Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are healthy, the Bengals have little trouble matriculating the ball down the field.

articles.title: How Justin Tucker’s 89.1% career accuracy compares with Harrison Butker’s career-low 68.8% this season

articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs signed kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad on Wednesday, days after Harrison Butker missed two field goals in a loss at Seattle. Butker has made 11 of 16 attempts this season, a career-low 68.8%. Tucker, 36, owns an 89.1% career rate, second best in NFL history, but he has not kicked in the league since 2024. The Chiefs are 5-1, and head coach Andy Reid has not handed the job to anyone else. Still, a seven-time Pro Bowler now stands a few yards away from the man he might replace.Justin Tucker's 89.1% career rate against Butker's 68.8% this seasonJustin Tucker's number comes from a long stretch of work. Across 13 seasons in Baltimore he led the league at 94.6% in 2021 and posted a career-best 97.4% in 2016. His 417 made field goals rank 14th all time. He also once held the NFL record with a 66-yarder against Detroit. That is what a team is buying when it wants certainty.Butker's 68.8% is a different kind of figure. It covers only six games, so one clean weekend could move it a lot. But the drop is steep. He made 86.8% in 2025 and 88.4% from 2017 through 2025. This year he sits almost 20 points below his own norm.Butker began the season third all time, behind Tucker and Cameron Dicker. Now he is working against his own record. The sample is small enough that a recovery is still possible, but the Chiefs have seen enough to buy some insurance.Seattle showed the problemSunday night made it plain. Butker missed a 58-yard field goal at the end of the first half and a 45-yarder in the fourth quarter. Kansas City lost 20-3, so every point mattered.A 58-yarder is a long try for anyone. The 45-yarder is the one that should bother the Chiefs. He has also missed an extra point this year, and NBC Sports counts seven misses across his last 11 games.Reid did not dodge it afterward. "He's been one of the most consistent kickers in football." He added that Butker is a bit off and has to fix it.Butker has three Super Bowl rings in Kansas City. That history buys patience.Why Justin Tucker is on the practice squadTucker is not on the 53-man roster, and Butker's job is not in immediate danger. The Chiefs are 5-1, which gives them room to wait. They worked out three kickers this week and picked Tucker over former Rams kicker Harrison Mevis.The résumé comes with questions. In 2024 Tucker went 22 of 30, or 73.3%, the worst season of his career. The NFL then suspended him for 10 games in 2025, and the Ravens released him in May of that year. Tucker has maintained that he did nothing inappropriate. Workouts followed with the Saints, Colts and Jets, but no contract.So the Chiefs are weighing a proven career against a rough last season and a long layoff. If Butker misses again, they will not have to start a search. Practice squad players can also be elevated for game days, so a switch would not take much paperwork.For now, Tucker practices and Butker kicks.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jonathan Taylor's Trade Stance Revealed by Colts' Shane Steichen After Nelson, Buckner Deals
articles.summary: In the aftermath of the Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner trades, Jonathan Taylor isn't trying to force his way off the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
In the aftermath of the Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner trades, Jonathan Taylor isn't trying to force his way off the Indianapolis Colts.

Colts head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Wednesday that Taylor has not requested a trade at this point.

When asked if Nelson or Buckner made a trade request, Steichen opted to keep it in house.

"I'll keep all of that private," he said.

Coming off three straight losses and the decision to fir e general manager Chris Ballard after a Week 6 defeat against the Tennessee Titans, the Colts officially entered sell mode on Tuesday.

Indianapolis started the day by sending Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks for two draft picks, including a 2027 third-round selection. Buckner followed a few hours later when he was traded to the San Francisco 49ers for a fourth-round pick in 2027.

Taylor is the biggest name the Colts could potentially move, though it's unclear how much activity there has been around him to this point.

The Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Minnesota Vikings, and Denver Broncos have been cited as teams that could have interest, but there's no indication any of them have put together a formal offer.

Per ESPN's Jordan Raanan , some people in the NFL believe the Colts will seek a second-round pick "and possibly more" if they trade Taylor.

Indianapolis is in a difficult spot right now with a 2-5 record and not having a first-round pick in the 2027 draft because it was traded to the New York Jets last year in the Sauce Gardner deal.

Based on the current standings , the Colts will be sending the No. 7 overall pick to the Jets. Their trades of Nelson and Buckner have them with a total of nine projected selections in the draft.

A key difference for Taylor compared to Nelson and Buckner is contract status. Nelson and Buckner are in the final season of their current deals and over the age of 30.

Taylor has two more years remaining on his contract beyond this season after signing a two-year, $44 million extension in August. He is one of the few bright spots for a struggling Colts team right now.

The three-time Pro Bowler ranks fifth in the NFL in rushing yards (587) and is tied for the league lead in rushing touchdowns (eight).

Despite Taylor's individual success since entering the league, he hasn't made the playoffs with the Colts since his rookie year in 2020. They haven't finished over .500 since 2023 (9-8).

The NFL trade deadline isn at 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 10 if the Colts want to make additional moves as they look toward the future amid a season that is quickly spiraling out of control.

articles.title: Tom Brady linked to Joan Smalls and Candice Swanepoel friendship fallout as model’s cryptic remarks spark questions
articles.summary: Joan Smalls and Candice Swanepoel are facing questions about their long friendship after comments linked to Smalls appeared on social media, with reports
articles.body: Joan Smalls and Candice Swanepoel are facing questions about their long friendship after comments linked to Smalls appeared on social media, with reports suggesting that NFL legend Tom Brady may be involved. The Victoria’s Secret models have reportedly fallen out after 15 years of friendship, while rumors about Swanepoel and Brady’s relationship have added to the speculation. However, the reason behind the reported disagreement has not been confirmed by either model, and the claims about Brady remain unverified.What happened between Joan Smalls and Candice Swanepoel? The “Backstabbers” comment explainedThe discussion began after fans noticed that Joan Smalls and Candice Swanepoel were not seen together at the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show, held in October. Social media users also noticed that the longtime friends no longer appeared to follow each other on Instagram, raising questions about whether something had changed between them.According to screenshots reported by entertainment outlets, a fan asked Smalls whether she was still friends with Swanepoel. The response attributed to Smalls read, “I’m not friends with backstabbers.”In another alleged comment, Smalls appeared to express deeper hurt over the end of a long friendship. She wrote, “There is no girl code with some people. And the disrespect and carelessness in how they treat you is so unimaginable. There’s no going back. Some people lack humility and a moral compass. And the way they gaslight, lie and minimize your feelings is the worst slap in the face after 15 yrs [of] friendship. Not a sorry said or written. Onwards and upwards!!!”The comments were reportedly deleted later, and their authenticity has not been independently confirmed. Smalls also responded to a Just Jared Instagram post discussing the alleged disagreement, writing, “Two words: SUMMER HOUSE ! That’ll explain everything.”Her reference appeared to point toward the Bravo reality show Summer House, which has featured a friendship dispute involving romantic relationships. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes comparison puts Caleb Williams in the spotlight after Terrell Owens reacts to Bears QB’s rapid rise
articles.summary: Caleb Williams is giving the Chicago Bears a reason to believe their offense can compete with the NFL’s best, and Hall of Fame wide receiver Terrell Owens
articles.body: Caleb Williams is giving the Chicago Bears a reason to believe their offense can compete with the NFL’s best, and Hall of Fame wide receiver Terrell Owens has noticed. After back-to-back 300-yard passing performances, Williams has drawn a striking comparison to Kansas City Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes. The timing matters. Williams missed three games with a hamstring injury, yet his return has brought fresh energy to Chicago’s playoff push. Owens believes the young quarterback is beginning to show why the Bears made him the No. 1 overall pick in 2024.Terrell Owens names Caleb Williams and Patrick Mahomes among NFL’s most dynamic QBsOwens shared his thoughts on Williams during his “Get TO The Point” podcast, praising the quarterback’s recent performances while making it clear that his playing ability matters far more than his personal style.“You already know. Number one. Paint my nail with this lip,” Owens said. “ This dude right here. Hey, Caleb, I paint my nails every weekend. Williams. The man, the Chicago Bears, these guys are balling. I don’t know what else to say about him. All I know is right now, he’s definitely special. This is his second week over 300 yards passing.“Painting nails or no painting nails, you cannot deny this guy’s ability and his talent. I think this is why they drafted him. I think at the end of last season, going into the playoffs, again, they should have gone further. Now you’re starting to see this guy really emerge. I think the game is starting to slow down.”Williams backed up that praise with a strong showing against the New England Patriots. He threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns in Chicago’s 30-24 win, helping the Bears improve to 5-2. The performance followed an equally impressive display against Atlanta, where he completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions.Those outings made Williams the first Bears quarterback to throw for more than 300 yards in consecutive games since Mitch Trubisky did it in three straight games in 2018.Owens then took the comparison further, putting Williams alongside one of the league’s most accomplished quarterbacks.“When you talk about dynamic quarterbacks, between him and Patrick Mahomes, these are the two most dynamic quarterbacks at that position,” Owens added.Caleb Williams’ progress gives Chicago more reasons for optimismThe comparison is about Caleb Williams’ style and potential, not a claim that he has already reached Mahomes’ level of achievement. His ability to create plays when protection breaks down, move outside the pocket and deliver difficult throws has caught attention. Now, he is also showing better control of the offense.That development could matter more to Chicago than any individual statistic. Williams has sometimes relied on his natural talent to escape pressure and extend plays. His recent performances suggest he is becoming more comfortable making quick decisions and working within the offense.The Bears have won four of their last five games, and Williams’ return has strengthened their position as they chase a playoff spot. He has also credited his offensive line and receivers for helping him succeed, a sign that he understands how much the team's performance depends on everyone doing their job.Mahomes remains the benchmark for quarterbacks who can change a game with both planned plays and improvisation. Williams still has plenty to prove over a full season, but Owens’ comments reflect a growing sense that Chicago may finally be seeing its young quarterback put everything together.The next test comes against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 8. Another strong performance would give Williams a chance to show that his recent surge is more than a brief hot streak.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Russell Wilson believes the Kansas City Chiefs should make a move for New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson after their 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on October 25. Wilson also noted that Mahomes looked unusually frustrated during the game, adding to concerns about the team’s passing attack.Russell Wilson wants the Kansas City Chiefs to trade for Garrett Wilson after Patrick Mahomes’ strugglesSpeaking on CBS Sports’ Set Hut, Russell Wilson made it clear that he sees Kansas City as a strong landing spot for Garrett Wilson, who signed a four-year, $130 million contract extension with the Jets in July 2025. The Cleveland Browns have been one of the biggest surprises of the 2026 season. Cleveland is 5-2 heading into Week 8 and sits atop the AFC North division standings alongside Pittsburgh. This shocking turn of events could impact how the Browns approach the upcoming NFL trade deadline .

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano shared intel from around the league in their latest article. They touched on how Cleveland could actually become buyers at the deadline after their hot start.

articles.title: Blake Cashman Named NFC Defensive Player of the Week
articles.summary: It’s getting to be a routine
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings played a football game this past Sunday. And, because it's now Wednesday, that means it's time for one of their players to be recognized with a weekly award from the National Football League.

The league has just announced that Vikings' linebacker Blake Cashman has been named the NFC's Defensive Player of the Week for Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season.

If it seemed like Cashman was all over the place in the Vikings' 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts this past Sunday, that's only because. . .well, he was. Cashman recorded 12 tackles on the afternoon, including eight solo tackles and two tackles for loss. He also had two quarterback sacks (a career high), three quarterback hits, and four passes defended. It was the twentieth game of his NFL career with at least ten tackles, and his sixteenth since joining the Vikings.

Sunday's game was also the seventeenth straight game where Cashman recorded at least seven tackles, which is the longest current streak in the NFL and the longest streak for a Viking dating back to at least 1987. He's the first player to have two sacks and four passes defended in a game since Alex Brown of the Chicago Bears did so in 2005, and the first player since at least 1982 (when the NFL first started recording sacks) to have at least twelve tackles, two sacks, and four passes defended in a game.

Seems like a pretty solid outing, all things considered.

We're now seven weeks into the season, and this is the fifth week where a member of the Vikings has been recognized with a weekly award. The only weeks where a Viking was not recognized were Week 1 when they defeated the Packers and Week 6 when they were on their bye week. Cornerback Isaiah Rodgers, return specialist Myles Price, and kicker Will Reichard were named NFC Special Teams Players of the Week in Weeks 2, 3, and 4, respectively (with Price being named the NFC's Special Teams Player of the Month for September for good measure), with cornerback Byron Murphy being recognized as the NFC's Defensive Player of the Week in Week 5.

Congratulations to Blake Cashman for being named the NFC's Defensive Player of the Week for Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season!

articles.title: 'Football 301' on NFL trade deadline: Jags WR Brian Thomas Jr., Titans RB Tony Pollard and 4 other players to watch
articles.summary: On a recent episode of Yahoo Sports' "Football 301" podcast, host Nate Tice and guest Gregg Rosenthal of the "NFL Daily" podcast offered their perspectives o...
articles.body:
As the NFL trade deadline approaches, speculation is ramping up about which players could be changing teams to reshape playoff races — or accelerate rebuilds. On a recent episode of Yahoo Sports' "Football 301" podcast, host Nate Tice and guest Gregg Rosenthal of the "NFL Daily" podcast offered their perspectives on top targets, ideal landing spots and what contending teams must consider before making a deal.

Here's a breakdown of players to watch, with a look at the ideas and analysis brought forward by Tice and Rosenthal.

Rosenthal highlighted BTJ as underutilized in Jacksonville, making him a prime trade deadline candidate. Thomas could unlock explosiveness for receiver-needy contenders like the Ravens or Chiefs, noting that his rookie contract increases his trade value.

The Rams were also mentioned as a potential "scheme fit" due to their need for speed, as they're currently "the most station-to-station offense in the league right now, which is crazy to think for a team quarterbacked by Matthew Stafford," Rosenthal said.

His ultimate landing spot for Thomas is Baltimore.

"How about let's just put BTJ, Zay Flowers and Lamar [Jackson] on the field together, and let's have some fun," Rosenthal said.

One concept discussed was sending Pollard to the Vikings, who need juice in their running game with Aaron Jones Sr. banged up (knee) and Jordan Mason underwhelming.

Tice noted Pollard's age (29) and expiring contract make him an attainable option for teams aiming to boost rushing production without a long-term commitment. Tice also weighed the trade dynamics of other backs (Saquon Barkley, Jonathan Taylor), ultimately viewing Pollard as the easiest to pry away without getting into complicated negotiations.

"I still have optimism about the Vikings' offense, but they need guys, I think, on the ground that can just create some stuff just to boost their offensive line a little bit," Tice said.

Tice spotlighted Baker as a fit for the Bills, who have been gashed in the secondary and need a tone-setter in the middle of the field. Baker's versatility and aggression would mesh with Buffalo's scheme.

"Budda Baker can give them a guy that can play in the box, a guy that can run up and help both ways, pass and run, and also fit in [coordinator] Jim Leonard's defense."

Greenard was offered up as a candidate for the Chiefs, a team looking to add pass-rushing heat. Rosenthal acknowledged the contract hurdles (notably Greenard's guaranteed money), but argued Kansas City's defense could accommodate another edge presence for a stretch run.

Rosenthal called Ojomo "the prize" among Eagles defenders likely to be dangled, suggesting a match with the Jaguars. The move would inject quickness and interior disruption alongside DaVon Hamilton and help offset lackluster pass rush production.

Stewart emerged as another Bills candidate for Tice. He's a two-down space eater who could fortify Buffalo's run defense and allow the team's gap-shooters to roam freely. It's a low-cost, high-impact transaction at a position of need for contenders.

The New York Giants could potentially be in the market for Jonathan Taylor should the Indianapolis Colts decide to move the star running back amid their ongoing fire sale.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Wednesday the Giants are "looking for" a running back and defensive tackle ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

Schultz's report comes after the Colts began a roster teardown by trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner on Tuesday.

Giants general manager Joe Schoen told reporters Tuesday he had been in contact with "teams that have already started some trades."

ESPN's Jordan Raanan previously reported the asking price for Taylor is expected to be "a second-round pick and possibly more."

Schoen said those early talks had given him "a pretty good idea who may or may not be available."

"It's got to make sense, short-term and long-term, when you make those moves," Schoen said.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday wide receiver Josh Downs had requested a trade from the Colts. Head coach Shane Steichen said Taylor had not as of the same day.

Taylor is currently signed through the 2028 season. Schoen holds six picks, including first- and second-round selections, in the upcoming 2027 draft.

The Giants released Najee Harris last week after failing to get Cam Skattebo any touches in Week 6. Harris had expressed frustration with splitting touches with three other running backs prior to being cut.

Harbaugh said when asked about Harris' complaints regarding the four-man running back rotation he would "love" for the Giants to be in "a Derrick Henry circumstance or a Saquon Barkley circumstance."

"Our run game hasn't earned that yet, and none of those guys have," Harbaugh said ahead of Week 7.

The Giants have stayed in playoff contention despite losing Jaxson Dart in part because of the relatively weak NFC East and in part because J.J. McCarthy led his team to an overtime win against the Houston Texans when making his first Giants start in Week 7.

The Athletic's Dan Duggan reported ahead of the game the Giants had decided to turn to McCarthy over Jameis Winston in part to make up for Dart's absence from the team's run game.

The Giants could hope further bolstering that rushing attack ahead of the deadline, potentially with a player Harbaugh can lean on to the degree he relied on Henry with the Ravens, will help the franchise stay in postseason contention long enough for Dart to potentially return for the playoffs.

articles.title: Justin Tucker joins the Kansas City Chiefs after a 10-game suspension last year for violating NFL conduct policy
articles.summary: Justin Tucker has joined the Kansas City Chiefs following a 10-game suspension for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy; he provides competition for their kicker Harrison Butker
articles.body:
Tucker spent 13 seasons with the Ravens, earning a reputation as one of the league's best kickers, before his tenure in Baltimore ended in controversy.

The Baltimore Banner reported in 2025 that he had been accused of sexual misconduct by 16 massage therapists at high-end spas, accusations that Tucker called "unequivocally false" and "tabloid fodder."

The Ravens released him that May and while Tucker was never criminally charged or sued in civil court, the NFL suspended him for the first 10 games of the 2025 season, which Tucker served as a free agent; he became eligible for reinstatement last November.

"He's done his suspension, you know? Took care of that business," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, "And I'll leave it at that".

Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker has struggled mightily the past two seasons, missing a pair of kicks in Sunday's loss in Seattle, and the signing of Tucker provides some competition for him even though Reid said Butker would kick on Sunday November 1 in Denver.

The Chiefs also worked out Ben Sauls and Harrison Mevis before giving Tucker the open spot on their practice squad.

"Listen, Harrison, we love. I've told you that before. He's one of my favourite guys," Reid said.

"Sometimes things don't go quite the way you want, and you work on that.

"He understands the business and how it works. We had a practice squad position open. Butker gets it. He knows that's part of the business. He's struggling a little bit and he gets it."

Butker has missed 10 field-goal attempts and five PATs since the start of last season, the most in the league, and they've come at quite a cost. He's the third-highest paid kicker in the league, carrying the sixth-highest base salary on the Kansas City roster.

Tucker, who turns 37 next month, had not been much better before he was released by Baltimore. He missed 10 kicks during the 2024 season, by far the most during a career that has included seven Pro Bowl selections.

The Chiefs have proven a willingness to give their players a second chance.

Last year, they brought back running back Kareem Hunt, whom the Chiefs had released years earlier after security footage showed him kicking a woman in a hotel hallway. They also signed current punter Matt Araiza, who was among multiple people accused of raping a woman at San Diego State.

Araiza claimed the encounters with the woman were consensual, the district attorney declined to file criminal charges, he later filed a defamation suit and pending cases were dropped with neither side admitting wrongdoing.

Asked what goes into making such decisions, Reid replied: "I try to do homework on it. See exactly what's taken place. (Tucker) served his suspension. Spent time involved in it. That's how I evaluate it."

Tucker also has had some run-ins with his new team-mates, including quarterback Patrick Mahomes and tight end Travis Kelce.

Two years ago, before the AFC championship game in Baltimore, the kicker was warming up in an area where Mahomes typically does his pregame work. The quarterback asked Tucker to move his gear, he responded by moving it ever-so slightly and Kelce promptly kicked his footballs and helmet away, leading to an exchange of words between them.

The Chiefs won the game 17-10, sending them back to the Super Bowl, where they beat San Francisco for their second straight title.

"It wasn't like we had any beef that moment," Mahomes said Wednesday. "At the end of the day, we're just playing a game. You want to compete and you want to win. But it's not like we had a longstanding beef that carries on. We won that game."

Butker also has courted controversy during his time in Kansas City, though it's been political rather than legal.

Several years ago, he made what he called a "very intentional" foray into politics when he delivered a polarising commencement address at Benedictine College in which Butker said, among other things, that most of the women receiving degrees were probably more excited about getting married and having children than beginning a professional career.

Butker later formed a political action committee for the 2024 election to encourage Christians to vote for "traditional values".

articles.title: Jahmyr Gibbs Reacts to Viral Video of Lions Celebrating After Packers Penalty in Rivalry Game
articles.summary: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs says his team's viral reaction to drawing a crucial offsides penalty in a Week 7 win over the Green Bay Packers can be traced back to a tradition shared by himself and teammate Amon-Ra St. Brown.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs says his team's viral reaction to drawing a crucial offsides penalty in a Week 7 win over the Green Bay Packers can be traced back to a tradition shared by himself and teammate Amon-Ra St. Brown.

Gibbs said in a Wednesday appearance on ESPN's Pat McAfee Show he and St. Brown have been celebrating opponents' offsides calls with the same move since debuting it in practice two years ago.

"Ever since then, every time we draw them offsides, we do that dance," Gibbs said. "But this time, it was different. Everybody started doing something different. That was funny."

Wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa could be seen joining Gibbs and St. Brown in their dance as other teammates went through a range of reactions to the Packers jumping offsides on a Lions three-and-five with two minutes remaining in last Sunday's matchup.

The Lions earned an automatic first down on the play and went on to cap off the drive with a game-winning 22-yard field goal from Jake Bates.

The game-winning drive, which allowed the Lions to recover from a failed attempt by Gibbs to run in a fourth-and-1 the possession prior, helped the Lions improve to 4-2 and remain undefeated at home.

The Lions will now get a chance to make up some ground in the battle for the top of the NFC North with a Sunday matchup against the visiting Minnesota Vikings.

articles.title: Mike McDaniel to Continue Calling Plays for Chargers Despite 0-6 Record with Justin Herbert
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh confirmed to reporters on Wednesday that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will continue to call plays despite the offense's struggles during an 0-6 start to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh confirmed to reporters on Wednesday that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will continue to call plays despite the offense's struggles during an 0-6 start to the 2026 season.

"We're very confident in Mike and his talent, work ethic, and ability," Harbaugh added . "And continue to be."

Javonte Carries Cowboys Back Into Race 😤

Harbaugh previously said he would be examining the offense during the team's bye week.

"We're looking into everything at this point, and that process is ongoing," he told reporters on Oct. 19. "Particularly offensively, scoring more points, the different multiple situational ways we need to play more complimentary football."

The Chargers currently rank 28th in passing (168.2 YPG), 13th in rushing (119 YPG) and 32nd in the NFL in scoring (15 PPG). Quarterback Justin Herbert is having a brutal season, throwing for 1,141 yards, five touchdowns and eight interceptions while taking 21 sacks and completing just 59.4 percent of his passes. It's been a massive disappointment.

There were some questions after McDaniel's hiring about how his offensive scheme might blend with Harbaugh's traditional approach to that side of the ball, but mostly excitement. Thus far, however, the combination has not proven to be fruitful.

How much longer McDaniel will keep his play-calling role if the losses continue to stack after the bye remains to be seen. For now, however, Harbaugh isn't making any sweeping changes in that regard.

articles.title: Madison Beer heckled by Chargers fans during Disney show, Madden impressions & Rays reporter Aileen Hnatiuk!
articles.summary: The final Hump Day of October brings Madison Beer hearing "Fix the Chargers!" from fans at Disneyland as Justin Herbert's NFL season spirals.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Final Hump Day of October, boys and girls. Feels like we just started what is, objectively, the greatest month of the year — and now it's just about over. Sad. You know what's even worse? An even bigger punch to the gut? CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Look at what I walked into at the Lowe's down the street yesterday afternoon: Disgusting behavior. I get it, by the way. Don't get me wrong. Save your, "This is how advertising works!" emails. I know. I gotcha. Doesn't make it any more palatable, though. Lowe's has already turned the page on Halloween. In fact, not pictured is the giant tent out in the parking lot that they've already got set up. That's the Christmas tree (!!!) tent, and it's been up since last week. As Mike Gundy once said, "Where are we at in society today?!" Anyway ... Welcome to a Hump Day Nightcaps — the one where Justin Herbert's fiancee, Madison Beer, hears it from sad Chargers fans during her performance at Disneyland. Happiest Place on Earth my butt! What else? I've also got Nic Cage portraying the late John Madden (I use 'portray' loosely), Rays fans under fire for being swallowed by Brewers fans, and OutKick legend Aileen Hnatiuk may have single-handedly willed Tampa to a Game 5 last night. You'll see. OK, grab you a pumpkin beer for our final Hump Day class of October, and let's get this show on the road. DOLPHINS AVOID 0-17 CRISIS, PICK UP FIRST WIN OF SEASON AGAINST STRUGGLING JETS ON THE ROAD Madison Beer's honeymoon is apparently over No stalling today. As I've said, time ain't our side right now. We've all got things to do and pumpkins to carve before Mariah Carey invades our homes for the next two months. So, let's start with the NFL ... If you would've told me in August that the Colts and Chargers would be the two most embarrassing teams in the league by Halloween, I would've said you were NUTS. I'd just naturally assume it was my Dolphins, but they've been more than respectable this season. Most ethical tank job of all time. Well done, Miami. Yesterday, the Colts started their fire-sale, and I assume the Chargers ain't far behind. They're coming off a bye week, and now get to play the Rams. When they lose, I wouldn't be surprised to see Mike McDaniel canned. ROB GRONKOWSKI CALLS CHARGERS 'PROBABLY THE BIGGEST MESS IN THE NFL' RIGHT NOW AFTER ROUGH START Even as a miserable Dolphins fan who was ready to see McDaniel go, I'll admit, I'm a little shocked at just how bad they've looked on offense this season. For years, the debate was, "Tua or Herbert?" The answer, it seems, is neither. They both stink. Trust me, I have a ton of Herbert in fantasy this year, and my teams STINK. He's looked genuinely terrible. Which brings me to his fiancée, Madison Beer ... Welcome to hell, Madison! And I ain't talking about Disneyland: Where do we rank this Madden impression? "FIX THE CHARGERS!" has got to be such a deflating thing to hear if you're Madison Beer performing at Disneyland. She signed on for a great season, and it's just been pure misery week in and week out. Madison and Herbert were all the rage in the offseason. We couldn't get enough of them. They had the NFL world wrapped around their fingers, and now she's having to deal with questions that should be directed at the front office. Sad. Chin up, Madison! Surely it can't get any worse, right ... Can't say I blame Justin here. Lord knows it's how I'd handle an 0-5 start. I respect the choice of beverage, too. Miller Lite is elite. Nobody does the aluminum bottle game better. Moving on ... Speaking of doing things better, let's check in with Nicolas Cage as his new John Madden biopic gets set to hit your Prime Video streams in just three shorts weeks! Aileen & the World Series I'm gonna level with everyone ... that's just an awful John Madden impression. I'm not sure we can even call it an impression? I think it's just Nicolas Cage ... talking like Nicolas Cage? He didn't even attempt to sound like Madden. I don't get it? And how about the dude playing Pat Summerall? He's getting a pass today because everyone is focused on how bad Cage's Madden is, but that's equally horrible. If you had me close my eyes and gave me a thousand guesses at who that was speaking, I would never land on John Madden. Ever. I'd say it was Nicolas Cage ... because it sounds like Nicolas Cage. For those too young to remember, this was peak John Madden: Goodness. Did we have it all, or what? Those were the days. Our family grew up eating turducken on Thanksgiving, and it was all because of Madden. He was the best. PS: Turducken? Good. The process of putting it together? Disgusting. But still, you do it right, and it's delicious. OK, let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a one final October Hump Day night. First up? I'll be the first to admit, I was wrong about this World Series. I figured Fox would get slammed in the ratings with the Rays and Brewers, but the numbers are out, and they're actually really solid: Look, they aren't Yankees or Dodgers numbers — or Phillies, Red Sox or Cubs — but it's a really strong start. Over 12 million for Game 1, and nearly 11 million for Game 2? I'd that in a heartbeat, especially given Game 2 went up against college football. Game 3 will be interesting to watch because it went up against Cowboys-Eagles. There's a reason the Cowboys are in primetime six times a year. But still, this is a win for for MLB. Not really a win for the owners, though. The whole "small market teams can't compete, on and off the field" argument has sort of fallen apart this postseason. I just think it's gonna be a tough sell when the lockout inevitably begins in five weeks. Sadly, I think that means we're in for a really long offseason. We'll see. Next? While the TV ratings look good, the optics inside the Trop on Monday ... did not: Lordy. That's A LOT of Brew Crew on my screen. A lot. I know it was a blowout. I know it's a big park. But still, I can't imagine Rays ownership loved seeing that. But hey! We've got a Game 5 tonight. Still time to show out, Rays fans! Let's extend this season to a Game 6, fellas. Again, it might be the last time we get baseball for a while. OK, that's it for today. Good final October Hump Day, everyone. Solid work. Welcome back, Aileen. See you tomorrow.

articles.title: Jets' Garrett Wilson Won't Request Trade, NFL Insider Calls Out 'Baseless' Rumors
articles.summary: Despite the New York Jets' struggles this year, Garrett Wilson has no plans to ask for a trade.
articles.body:
Despite the New York Jets' struggles this year, Garrett Wilson has no plans to ask for a trade.

The star wide receiver said he hasn't and won't ask for a trade, and said he wants to be in New York. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport noted that "baseless trade speculation" has gone "nuts" leading up to the deadline.

Why Jets Are Sneaky Winner of Colts Trade 😏

Wilson said he ultimately values winning more than staying with the Jets, but he's "hopeful" about what they're building.

"I want to win games and that's the one thing we've been missing on here," he told reporters . "I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I'm hopeful."

The fact that Wilson's name is coming up in trade speculation shouldn't be much of a surprise, considering he's one of the team's most valuable pieces and the Jets are more likely to be sellers than buyers.

Wilson, who is in his fifth season with the Jets, has recorded 444 yards and three touchdowns on 37 receptions so far this year. Amid a rough game against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, Wilson appeared to be having a heated conversation with quarterback Geno Smith, only adding to speculation that he could be unhappy.

Head coach Aaron Glenn downplayed that altercation.

"Well, I think sometimes that's overblown as far as what people think is happening," Glenn told reporters . "Sometimes those conversations could be totally something else. And, listen, I know for a fact that Geno and Garrett, it was more or less, 'Man, let's get going and let's get the offense going' more than guys bickering at each other. I know what type of player Garrett is. I know what type of player Geno is, and I know where their heart's at, too."

Wilson also addressed the conversation after the game, saying he and Smith "were collaborating."

Despite never having reached the playoffs during his time in New York, Wilson has been, somewhat surprisingly, optimistic about the team. He called the Jets' playoff chances "very realistic" before the start of the season.

"I mean, I think it should happen, I'll say that," Wilson said in September. "It's our job to go play ball and do it, but that's how I feel about it."

The Jets are now 2-5 and still have some of their toughest opponents ahead of them, so it makes sense for New York to trade some of its pieces before the deadline as it looks to build for the future.

Whether Wilson will be on the move remains to be seen.

articles.title: Chiefs coach defends signing kicker who was suspended after sexual misconduct allegations
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid offered only a short explanation Wednesday when asked why the team was comfortable signing kicker Justin Tucker, who has not played in the NFL since 2024 after a string of sexual misconduct allegations.
articles.body: Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid offered only a short explanation Wednesday when asked why the team was comfortable signing kicker Justin Tucker, who has not played in the NFL since 2024 after a string of sexual misconduct allegations. “He’s done his suspension. Took care of his business there. I’ll leave it at that,” Reid said when asked what message the signing of Tucker sent to female fans. When asked what level of involvement team ownership had in the signing, Reid added: “We try to do our homework best way we possibly can, and talk to a lot of people, and make sure things are okay.” On Wednesday, the Chiefs signed Tucker, 37, to their practice squad. Kansas City was looking for competition at the kicking position due the poor performance of starting kicker Harrison Butker, who has missed five of his 16 field-goal attempts so far this season. Tucker last played for the Baltimore Ravens during the 2024 season. In January 2025, The Baltimore Banner reported accounts from six women who accused Tucker of nonconsensual sexual behavior during massage therapy sessions between 2012 and 2016, including that he exposed his genitals and brushed women with his exposed penis. The following month, 10 more massage therapists came forward with more accusations against Tucker. The kicker denied all allegations at the time, initially describing them as “unequivocally false.” “I maintain I did not act inappropriately at any point before, during, or after a professional bodywork treatment session, nor have I ever been told I am unwelcome at any massage therapy provider. These claims are simply not true,” Tucker said in a statement in February 2025. “It devastates me to know that anyone I have worked with would not have felt respected and valued as a professional, but more importantly as a person, and to anyone who has felt otherwise, I am sorry,” Tucker added. The NFL suspended Tucker for the first 10 weeks of the 2025 NFL season following an investigation into the accusations, but he remained unsigned for the entire season. Earlier this year, Tucker worked out with the Miami Dolphins, according to NFL reporter Aaron Wilson. When asked about his decision-making process when it comes to signing a player such as Tucker, Reid said, “I try to do homework on it, see exactly what’s taken place since. He served a suspension, there’s been time involved with it. That’s how I evaluate it.” When asked the kind of homework he did on Tucker, Reid said, “I’m not going to get into all of that.” Reporters also asked Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes about the signing Wednesday, and he expressed confidence in the team’s front office. “We had a lot of people that we’ve added in and out,” Mahomes said, per ESPN. “I try not to get too high or too low on anything. I know [general manager Brett] Veach [and the front office] do a great job of bringing great players in. But for me, it was about the Denver Broncos and moving on and continuing to get better.” Tucker is second all-time in the NFL in field-goal kicking percentage. He struggled during his final season with the Ravens, however, converting a career-worst 73.3% of his field goals.

Los Angeles Chargers safety Derwin James Jr. could be headed for injured reserve.

Coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters the five-time Pro Bowler experienced a setback as he recovers from a hamstring injury. That could leave the team with no choice but to use an IR designation.

The situation sums up the Chargers' entire season.

Yet again, injuries to key players are dooming whatever grand ambitions the Chargers had. At 0-6, they'll be lucky to simply make the playoffs.

Shifting the veteran defensive back to injured reserve would rule him out until a Week 12 matchup with the New England Patriots at the earliest.

articles.title: Mel Kiper Jr. Ranks His Top-5 WR's in 2027 NFL Draft Class Amid Jeremiah Smith, Charlie Becker Buzz

Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith and Indiana's Charlie Becker headlined ESPN draft analyst Mel Kiper Jr.'s list of the top five wide receivers in the 2027 NFL draft class.

Kiper unveiled his rankings during a Wednesday appearance on First Draft .

Mel Kiper Jr.'s Top Five Wide Receivers in the 2027 NFL Draft

articles.title: Justin Tucker: Kansas City Chiefs defend decision to sign kicker to practice squad
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid defends the franchise's decision to sign Justin Tucker to its practice squad, stating the kicker has "done his suspension".
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid has defended the decision to sign Justin Tucker to their practice squad, stating the kicker has "done his suspension".

Tucker, one of the most accurate kickers in NFL history, was last year accused of sexual misconduct , external by 16 massage therapists in the Baltimore area during the 2010s.

The 36-year-old - who won Super Bowl XLVII with the Baltimore Ravens - has consistently denied the allegations and never faced criminal charges.

Following an investigation, Tucker received a 10-game suspension , external from the NFL for violating the league's personal conduct policy.

He was released by Baltimore in May 2025 in what they described as a "football decision" following declining form.

Having served the ban last season, Tucker is immediately available for selection.

Reid said in a news conference on Wednesday: "He's done his suspension, taking care of that business there. I'll leave it at that.

"We try to do our homework the best way we possibly can and talk to a lot of people, make sure things are okay."

Pressed on what he meant by "homework", Reid added: "I'm not going to get into all that. To bring him here, I did some homework.

"He's here and he's on the practice squad, so we roll with it."

Tucker, a five-time All-Pro, is second in NFL history in field-goal percentage, making 89.1% of his attempts across 13 seasons, but endured the worst season of his career in 2024, kicking just 73.3% of his field-goal attempts.

The Chiefs made their move for him following a run of poor form by Harrison Butker, who has been the team's kicker since 2017 and has the fifth-best accuracy (87.3%) in NFL history.

However, the 31-year-old has missed five of his 16 field-goal attempts this season, including two from three in a 20-3 defeat by the Seattle Seahawks on Saturday.

articles.title: Myles Garrett Injury Status, Return Timeline Updated By Rams' Sean McVay Amid Knee Issue
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay revealed Wednesday that Myles Garrett's 21-day practice window won't be opened this week, according to Stu Jackson of the team's official website.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay revealed Wednesday that Myles Garrett's 21-day practice window won't be opened this week, according to Stu Jackson of the team's official website.

McVay also explained that Garrett is "on a week-to-week basis," per Jackson.

On Sept. 17, the Rams placed the star pass-rusher on injured reserve after he underwent arthroscopic surgery on his left knee.

Garrett has already missed four weeks since the placement, meaning that he's eligible to be activated off IR and make his return whenever he's ready to suit up again.

It initially appeared as though the Rams could open his 21-day practice window ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers, as NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Friday that it was "likely" Garrett returned to practice in the week leading up to the contest.

Jonathan Jones of The Athletic previously reported that a six-week recovery timeline for the 30-year-old was viewed as a "worst-case scenario" as well.

Garrett will be sidelined for a little while longer, however.

The Rams had high expectations entering their 2026 campaign, as they acquired Garrett in a blockbuster trade with the Cleveland Browns in June. The two-time Defensive Player of the Year was also coming off a 2025 season in which he set a new NFL record with 23 sacks.

Garrett's inaugural year in Los Angeles hasn't started on a high note, as he has yet to share the field with Aaron Donald after the star defensive tackle came out of retirement to join the Rams once again.

Los Angeles currently sits at No. 3 in the NFC West standings with a 3-4 record.

Garrett's next opportunity to return will come against the Washington Commanders on Nov. 8.

articles.title: Eagles' Saquon Barkley Weighs In On Potential 18-Game NFL Season Amid Injury Concerns
articles.summary: Count Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley among those who are against the NFL expanding to 18 regular-season games.
articles.body:
Count Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley among those who are against the NFL expanding to 18 regular-season games.

"I can't speak on how players feel," Barkley told Dan Roberts of Front Office Sports (9:55 mark). "How do I feel about it? I'm not a fan of it. I actually don't agree with it, to be completely honest.

"Yeah, and so if it's up to me and up to my vote on that particular thing that they want to change, I don't think so. … I'm all about players' health. And I don't see how any way adding another game is advantageous to our health for the now and for the future."

He highlighted the physical wear and tear of the sport, including at his running back position.

"But me personally, if you talk about the best way I can answer it for player safety, I don't see how adding another game is good for player safety," Barkley continued. "And that's just kind of my stance on it. But I know some people agree and a lot of people disagree with it."

The comments were particularly notable coming from Barkley, who has dealt with a hamstring injury this season.

Mark Maske of Front Office Sports noted the league and team owners are eventually expected to propose expanding the regular-season schedule to 18 games, although any official discussions are on hold while JC Tretter, who is the union's executive director, talks to players on team visits.

The NFL expanded to 17 games starting with the 2021 season.

In March, ESPN's Stephen Holder reported the NFLPA took a public stance against expanding the schedule to 18 games. However, Holder pointed out it did so before the schedule expanded to 17 games as well before eventually agreeing to a new collective bargaining agreement.

If the league wanted to expand the schedule again before the current CBA expires after the 2030 season, it would have to negotiate with the union and surely offer other concessions.

For now, it is just something that has been speculated about and discussed, and Barkley was clear where he stood.

articles.title: Davante Adams Injury Return Timeline Updated By Rams' Sean McVay After Hamstring Surgery
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams could return to the team sooner than initially feared.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams could return to the team sooner than initially feared.

Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters Wednesday that Adams underwent surgery on his hamstring and is expected to return "on the shorter end" of his six-to-10 week estimated timeline. McVay said that estimation was "based on how everything went" with the clean out surgery.

Adams suffered the injury during the Rams' loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 18 and missed their most recent victory over his former team in the Las Vegas Raiders.

The six-time Pro Bowler led the NFL with 14 touchdown catches last season and was off to a solid start this year with 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns in six games. He exploded for 195 yards and two scores against the New York Giants in Week 2 and followed up with 137 yards through the air in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos.

Despite this setback, Adams has been fairly durable throughout his career. He has never played fewer than 12 games in a season since he entered the league as a second-round draft pick in 2014.

Adams is one of the best wide receivers of his generation with six seasons of more than 1,000 receiving yards and seven seasons of double-digit touchdown catches. He has led the league in touchdown catches three different times.

That he has remained so effective even in the latter portion of his career is one reason the Rams reached the NFC Championship Game last season and were on the short list of realistic contenders coming into the 2026 campaign.

However, Los Angeles will now have to adjust to life without him on the field for more than a month. That adjustment started off well with the blowout win over the Raiders, and the next three games before the bye are against teams that have struggled in the Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders and Cardinals.

Matthew Stafford and Puka Nacua should be enough to keep the aerial attack rolling against those opponents, but the Rams will be far more dangerous when Adams does return.
