The second wave of allegations accused Tucker of "acting inappropriately" at some of the best luxury spas in Baltimore, including the spas at the Four Seasons and Ritz-Carlton Residences in the city. Tucker denied all accusations in a statement to OutKick last year. "I maintain I did not act inappropriately at any point before, during, or after a professional bodywork treatment session, nor have I ever been told I am unwelcome at any massage therapy provider," he said. "These claims are simply not true." He added at the time that he was recounting 13 years of experiences with bodywork professionals. "I can assure whoever is reading this that I have never intended to disrespect anyone, cross any boundary, or make anyone feel uncomfortable in any way whatsoever. "It devastates me to know that anyone I have worked with would not have felt respected and valued as a professional, but more importantly as a person, and to anyone who has felt otherwise, I am sorry," Tucker said in his statement, the full text of which can be found below. "I want you to know I am committed to ensuring that everyone I interact with continues to feel that I respect them and care about them as a human being." The Ravens cut ties with Tucker after 13 seasons in May 2025, saying it was a "football decision." Tucker was never criminally charged or sued civilly over the allegations, but the allegations, and subsequent NFL suspension, led some to compare him to Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson. Both of their cases involved allegations from multiple female massage therapists, with Watson facing an 11-game suspension in 2022. The Chiefs’ history with controversial players includes wide receiver Rashee Rice, who was involved in a multi-vehicle crash in Dallas in March 2024, leading to felony charges. He served jail time this offseason after violating his probation. In the past, running back Kareem Hunt was cut by the Chiefs after surveillance video surfaced of a domestic dispute with a woman in a hotel hallway. He served an eight-game suspension in March 2019, though the Chiefs re-signed him in 2024. He spent the last two seasons with Kansas City, playing 30 games. At the time of his re-signing, head coach Andy Reid said that the running back matured, took accountability and deserved a second chance with the club. Tyreek Hill was also a polarizing receiver who faced a 2014 domestic assault case that was dismissed and a 2019 child abuse probe, though no charges were filed. And while it isn’t a legal situation, Butker fell into controversial waters after delivering his commencement speech at Benedictine College, where he criticized Pride Month, abortion policies and traditional career roles for women, which drew widespread media reaction and caused Reid and others to field questions about his cultural stances. On the field, the Chiefs suffered their first loss at the hands of the Seattle Seahawks on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 7. They still lead the AFC West with a 5-1 record, and look like a team ready to compete for the Lombardi Trophy once more. He is tied for the most missed field goals in the NFL this season with five. Tucker, who turns 37 next month, had his worst statistical season of his career in 2024, making only 73.3% of his field goal attempts, which is a career-low. However, he is one of the most decorated at his position to ever play the sport, tallying five first-team nods and seven Pro Bowls. articles.title: Colts’ Sauce Gardner on Nelson, Buckner trades: ‘It hurt’
articles.summary: Colts CB Sauce Gardner spoke on the emotional departures of Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and shared his message for the team moving forward.
articles.body:
Sauce Gardner admitted the unfortunate part of business in the NFL as the Indianapolis Colts trade two of their team captains on Tuesday.

Speaking with reporters Wednesday, the Colts cornerback addressed the departures of Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner — and the emotional impact of losing both players within hours of each other.

"It was one of those things like, it hurt, it hurt for sure because like I said those are two captains that embodied everything, two great players and great people. … It was a little crazy for sure," Gardner said, via Roundtable.io's Jake Arthur .

Indianapolis traded Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection. Buckner went to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick. The moves added future draft capital while exposing potential issues on both sides of the line of scrimmage.

The losses for Gardner aren't simply tied to what Nelson and Buckner contributed on Sundays.

His description of the departing captains noted the team's understanding of relinquishing their first-rate capabilities on the field, in addition to creating a leadership void.

Nelson and Buckner had each been voted a team captain in six consecutive seasons. Their departures come with Indianapolis sitting at 2-5 and preparing to face the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday.

Gardner, however, made clear that the trades haven't changed what the current players expect of themselves.

"We want to dominate each and every game we go out there and play. That's our message."

That standard will be put to the test quickly. The Colts must prepare for a division opponent Sunday against the 4-2 Jacksonville Jaguars, whose defense ranks third in the NFL in points allowed at 17.3 per game.

articles.title: Jets CB Talks Potential Trade Request, 'Definitely Frustrated' with Role After New Contract
articles.summary: New York Jets cornerback Nahshon Wright revealed that he's "definitely frustrated" with his role on the team's defense despite not officially requesting a trade yet, according to ESPN's Rich Cimini.
articles.body:
New York Jets cornerback Nahshon Wright revealed that he's "definitely frustrated" with his role on the team's defense despite not officially requesting a trade yet, according to ESPN's Rich Cimini .

"Not formally...(But) I've expressed my feelings (to the team)," Wright said, per Cimini.

He signed a fully guaranteed one-year contract worth $3.5 million with the Jets in May, but has primarily operated as a depth option this season.

"I'm open to anything at this point," Wright said, per Cimini . "I just want to go where I can play, whether it's here or somewhere else. I just want to contribute. I know what I can do and I think I put that on display [last season]. So, yeah, it's definitely frustrating."

articles.title: Brian Thomas Jr. Reacts to NFL Trade Rumors Amid Diminished Role in Jaguars Offense
articles.summary: Brian Thomas Jr. isn't sweating any trade rumors as he continues to have a background role in the Jacksonville Jaguars' offense.
articles.body:
Brian Thomas Jr. isn't sweating any trade rumors as he continues to have a background role in the Jacksonville Jaguars' offense.

"Everybody's entitled to their own opinion," he told reporters Wednesday. "I just go out there, do what I do, and just try to go out there and be the best player I can be."

Thomas, 24, was a Pro Bowler as a rookie after catching 87 passes for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns. But he struggled last season, pulling in just 48 receptions for 707 yards and two touchdowns last year, calling into question whether he was a good fit in Liam Coen's offense.

Those doubts have lingered into 2026, with Thomas managing just nine catches for 105 yards and a touchdown in six games. It wouldn't be a surprise if the Jaguars ultimately chose to move him, though for now he's worried about the things he can control.

"Everybody goes through adversity," Thomas told reporters. "You've just got to keep fighting through it. That's the only way I know how to get through, just keep fighting through it. And that's what I'm going to continue to do, keep fighting and keep coming in with a good mindset, keep working hard each and every day at practice. Going out there, doing the little things, trying to be the best that I can be, blocking, doing all the little things, just keep fighting through it."
